Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo is warning about increasingly autonomous AI, recursive improvement, concentration of power and ultimately the question:  WHO ACTUALLY CONTROLS THE AI?  @BobbyO_ has been approaching the same problem from another direction.  WHAT INFRASTRUCTURE CONTROLS WHAT AN AI AGENT IS ACTUALLY ALLOWED TO DO?  That distinction is enormous.  AI is rapidly moving from:  💬 Answering questions  to  💻 Writing code  to  🤖 Operating applications  to  ⚙️ Executing actions  to potentially  🧠 Conducting increasingly autonomous research and development.  And we’re already seeing warnings in the REAL WORLD.  🚨 GitLab patched a critical AI Gateway vulnerability where an authenticated Duo Agent user could potentially escape a prompt-template sandbox and execute commands.  🚨 Apple is strengthening controls around Full Disk Access as increasingly capable AI agents create new privacy risks.  🚨 DIVD has described an agentic cyberattack where attackers chained two zero-days, ultimately enabling privilege escalation from a Zammad user to ROOT.  Different incidents.  Same underlying lesson.  PROMPTS ARE NOT PERMISSION SYSTEMS.  Telling an agent:  “Don’t access this.”  “Don’t execute that.”  “Don’t transfer this.”  is fundamentally different from engineering infrastructure where:  🔐 THE AGENT DOESN’T HAVE THE AUTHORITY.  And THIS is where BobbieO’s $ICP argument becomes extremely interesting.  Imagine autonomous agents operating through:  ♾️ Cryptographic identities  ♾️ Canister-level permissions  ♾️ Explicit authorization  ♾️ Isolated application logic  ♾️ Threshold cryptography  ♾️ Human approval for sensitive actions  ♾️ Multisig authorization  ♾️ Governance-controlled authority  ♾️ Verifiable application logic and state  The model can THINK.  The model can REASON.  The model can PROPOSE.  But the infrastructure determines what it can actually EXECUTE.  AI INTELLIGENCE ⬇️ CRYPTOGRAPHIC IDENTITY ⬇️ PROGRAMMABLE AUTHORITY ⬇️ VERIFIABLE RULES ⬇️ AUTHORIZATION ⬇️ EXECUTION  That does NOT mean $ICP solves AI alignment or makes software invulnerable.  It doesn’t.  This is about something much more practical:  BUILDING HARD DIGITAL BOUNDARIES AROUND AUTONOMOUS SOFTWARE.  Because the question of the AI era won’t simply be:  HOW INTELLIGENT IS THE AGENT?  It will increasingly become:  WHO CONTROLS IT?  WHAT CAN IT ACCESS?  WHAT CAN IT EXECUTE?  WHO CAN OVERRIDE IT?  AND WHO HOLDS THE KEYS?  🚨 BEFORE WE GIVE AUTONOMOUS AI CONTROL OF THE DIGITAL WORLD, WE NEED INFRASTRUCTURE THAT CONTROLS WHAT AI IS ACTUALLY ALLOWED TO DO.  That is where BobbieO’s argument deserves serious attention.  And that is where the architecture of Internet Computer could become VERY important.  ♾️ AI + PROGRAMMABLE AUTHORITY + VERIFIABLE COMPUTE + ON-CHAIN STATE. Kernel maintainers now auto‑assign a CVE to every back‑ported fix. As one commenter put it: “_any_ bugfix is assigned a cve.” The result? A firehose of IDs that drowns triage for maintainers.
The advisory covers the stable trixie release, patched in linux 6.12.111‑1. 1,313 CVEs — mostly memory‑safety bugs in drivers, net, BPF, io_uring — all get a CVE by default. for every fix.

Debian just dropped a kernel advisory with 1,313 CVEs in one shot. The list stretches across three years of future‑dated IDs. 👇 It's a flood that makes the CVE system look like a firehose and drowns maintainers.

My thoughts on initial vector identification are similar to my thoughts on attribution. You consider level of effort, level of granularity, and level of confidence necessary. If there's seven unpatched vulnerabilities that enable remote code execution in an internet facing technology, and you can't easily tell which was exploited, but you do know that the entry point was that server, how much effort will you spend on high confidence CVE linkage?  There's some post-exploitation IOCs being shared that were valid IOCs for intrusions that  have occurred in the past for one or more CVEs. Specific paths being used by adversaries is interesting and you should of course care about ANY webshells on your edge devices, but be cautious about leaping to the conclusion that webshell plus path is conclusive evidence of a specific vulnerability being exploited. Yet, this is sort of the point. It's not like if there's five vulnerabilities and you determine it was vulnerability 3 that you're going to just ignore the other four.   There's going to be more and more vulnerabilities, but post-exploitation behaviors are often agnostic of the vulnerability exploited (again, not an absolute and with some nuance), so you want to have a strong hardening and detection game that's not dependent on detecting hyper specific CVEs.

If I had 6 months to break into cybersecurity in the AI era.  Here’s exactly how I’d spend those 6 months.  Stage 1: Linux and Networking  Learn: Linux, TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, TLS, SSH, firewalls, sockets. Practice: Build a network lab with multiple VMs and analyze traffic with Wireshark. Why: Security starts with understanding how systems communicate.  Stage 2: Web & API Security  Learn: OWASP Top 10, authentication, sessions, SQLi, XSS, SSRF, CSRF, IDOR. Practice: Build a vulnerable API, exploit it, then secure it. Why: Most modern applications are exposed through APIs.  Stage 3: Identity & Access  Learn: OAuth2, OIDC, JWT, RBAC, MFA, API keys, secrets management. Practice: Build an auth service with role-based permissions and audit logs. Why: A compromised identity can bypass almost every other security layer.  Stage 4: Cloud Security  Learn: AWS IAM, VPCs, security groups, KMS, CloudTrail, S3 security. Practice: Deploy an application with least-privilege IAM and private networking. Why: Your security perimeter is increasingly in the cloud.  Stage 5: Detection & Incident Response  Learn: SIEM, log analysis, threat intelligence, MITRE ATT&CK, incident response. Practice: Generate an attack, collect the telemetry and investigate it end-to-end. Why: Prevention fails. You need to know when you've been breached.  Stage 6: DevSecOps  Learn: SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, secret detection, container security, IaC scanning. Practice: Build a CI/CD pipeline that automatically blocks vulnerable builds. Why: Security can't be a final step before production.  Stage 7: Network & Application Defense  Learn: WAFs, reverse proxies, rate limiting, network segmentation, mTLS, Zero Trust. Practice: Secure a microservices application with service-to-service authentication. Why: Modern systems have hundreds of moving parts and trust boundaries.  Stage 8: Cloud & Container Hardening  Learn: Docker security, Kubernetes RBAC, pod security, image signing, runtime security. Practice: Harden a Kubernetes deployment and detect a compromised container. Why: Containers introduce a whole new attack surface.  Stage 9: AI Security  Learn: Prompt injection, data leakage, RAG security, tool abuse, model supply-chain risks. Practice: Attack an AI agent with access to tools and sensitive data. Why: An AI agent with excessive permissions can turn a prompt injection into a real security incident.  Stage 10: Security Automation  Learn: Python, APIs, SOAR concepts, automated remediation and threat detection. Practice: Build a system that detects suspicious activity and automatically isolates the affected resource. Why: Security teams can't investigate every alert manually.  Stage 11: Security Architecture  Learn: Threat modeling, attack trees, defense in depth, least privilege, risk analysis. Practice: Threat-model an AI SaaS before writing the code. Why: Fixing a security flaw in the architecture is cheaper than fixing it in production.  Stage 12: Portfolio & Real World Practice  Learn: CTFs, CVE analysis, security writeups, architecture diagrams. Practice: Build 3 projects: a vulnerable web app, a mini SOC, and a secure AI agent. Why: A GitHub full of certificates doesn't demonstrate that you can secure a system.  AI can generate code faster than ever. That also means insecure code can reach production faster. The modern security engineer needs to understand both:  how systems are built and how they can be broken.  Bookmark this roadmap and repost!

BPFDoor, Rekoobe, and a new Linux implant called AVERAT are hitting telecom edge appliances and mail-security gateways across South Korea 🇰🇷 and Taiwan 🇹🇼, using SMTP port 25 as C2 camouflage and fileless staging to survive on embedded devices with no on-disk trace.  Key findings:  - The attack chain opens with a dropper (SHA-256: 2bedc26d4b29b435c21962beed7db21188a0219a0d28334bba8b4fb1656d7b15) that derives its AES-128-ECB key from SHA1("ShareTech"), pointing squarely at ShareTech appliances. It copies two binaries from /addpkg/sbin/ into /sbin as ntpdate and udevds, executes them, then unlinks both within ten seconds. Both processes keep running without an on-disk image: /proc/pid/exe resolves to "(deleted)" and grepping /sbin finds nothing. The dropper re-executes as a watchdog and relies on the firmware's own package startup to survive reboots, so there is no persistence code to find. Gate artifacts to hunt: /tmp/flag (precondition), /HDD/ms6x2xTo64/updIptable.php (shell script disguised as PHP), and /HDD/ms6x2xTo64/execProcEnd (watchdog marker).  - AVERAT (six builds, all recovered from /sbin/udevds) connects outbound on TCP/25, issues EHLO and STARTTLS, then runs its own hand-rolled TLS session authenticated with magic value 1571 (0x0623). Check-ins occur every 600-699 seconds and persist the interval to a hidden state file: /var/lib/.db, /var/lib/.sencha, /var/lib/.us, or /var/lib/.a depending on build. The 276-byte encrypted config blob (RC4, key derived from its own first 16 bytes) holds three C2 host/port slots. C2 infrastructure splits between attacker-registered domains (mx.zxopfds[.]com, spam.suwaccqi[.]com, mx1.wwstifsteel[.]com) and hardcoded consumer-broadband IPs (59.125.211[.]65, 122.116.138[.]33, 1.34.200[.]85) confirmed as compromised Chunghwa Telecom HiNet (AS3462) CPE: a fuel retailer's Synology NAS, an end-of-life NetKlass SMB appliance, and a Dahua DH-XVR5116HS-I3 CCTV recorder. All three also run operator-installed PPTP on 1723 with a byte-identical banner, making each node a dual-purpose relay and VPN foothold. Command code 1618 opens a proxy or port-forward through the compromised appliance; the reboot handler (code 916) calls sync() before forcing a kernel restart, deliberately flushing volatile state while leaving disk persistence intact.  - The South Korean 🇰🇷 BPFDoor cluster (SHA-256: a37ea9897221d4495b538de72b74f2aa1d2ff09b7b6dcedd395aee58931adbf3 and 7e667ba5f9df912e02275d3cfe3809d16f822fe776f4035c84b118ebd925b1b5) uses magic bytes 0x6693 (UDP), 0x4274 (TCP), and 0x7820 (ICMP), passwords gZbpx0 (reverse shell) and sT21xf (bind shell), and impersonates /var/run/spamsniper.pid, directly naming SpamSniper anti-spam software as the masquerade target. The data-plane BPFDoor pair (a6f3b7f932761fb1fd5e74123f2482e36c65dd13e769af2ce08c65da195bfa7a and 4435fcd6862921092614dbeaa880e4192352984686ebcd98f0ba13ee8e226ef9) spoofs ora_ppmond and /sniper/snipe/bin/dtnpd respectively, integrating Tiny Shell with single-byte S/U/D commands for shell, upload, and download. The BPF Rekoobe sample (652508a9cf40bee883dc0e5e219dfeba71fe7dac591d01c89f74c21f73b4963f) sniffs for traffic where src port and dst port both equal 25, authenticated with a 32-byte magic sequence and XOR key uvTIgh47,[@]R, then spoofs /sniper/autorun/rblsmtpd to blend with a mail gateway's expected process list. On a SpamSniper appliance, a packet with src=25 dst=25 matches the legitimate MTA relay firewall rule and reaches the raw socket before stateful inspection.  - The updated BPFDoor controller now supports HTTPS POST tunneling (-g flag, dogetlogin function) to defeat static network signatures: it sends mathematically padded requests (e.g., POST /admin/login.aspx?id=99990) so the string "9999" lands at exactly offset 26 of the TCP payload as a dynamic reference point. The controller spoofs /usr/sbin/abrtd via PR_SET_NAME. New flags include -H for a hidden relay IP, -D to customize URI paths for log blending, and -v for debug output. MITRE ATT&CK techniques documented across both clusters include T1205.002 (Socket Filters), T1036.004/T1036.005 (Masquerading), T1070.003 (Clear Command History), T1071.003 (Mail Protocols), T1573.001 (Symmetric Cryptography), T1090 (Proxy), and T1584.008 (Compromise Infrastructure: Network Devices), among others in the report.  Takeaway for responders: File-based detection on these appliances will fail because nothing survives in /sbin. Hunt for Linux processes where /proc/pid/exe shows "(deleted)", inspect memory maps for executable pages with no backing file, and alert on the process-tree sequence of sh -c against a .php path followed by cp and chmod into /sbin then rm -rf of the same path within ten seconds. On the network, flag outbound TCP/25 from processes that are not mail services, especially where the destination resolves to consumer-grade CPE. Check for PPTP on 1723 on edge appliances that have no business running it. Full IOC tables, cryptographic constants, host artifacts, and YARA rules are available in the Rapid7 report and in Rapid7's Intelligence Hub.  #DFIR_Radar

BraZetsu: a Brazilian 🇧🇷 Python-based IAB framework attributed to threat actor Exilware targets Iberian and Latin American corporate, financial, industrial, and law enforcement environments, feeding a commercial access marketplace since February 2026.  Key findings:  - BraZetsu is a modular, Python 3 framework compiled with Nuitka into standalone PE executables, a choice that defeats signature-based detection and complicates reverse engineering. At time of analysis, the latest v5 build was fully undetectable on VirusTotal. The framework retrieves its C2 config as a Base64, XOR-encrypted blob from Pastebin dead-drop resolvers (e.g., hxxps://pastebin[.]com/raw/aF0WCxia), decoded with the hardcoded key p4st3_s3cr3t_k3y, then parses the c2_domain, port, and auth_token from a pipe-delimited string. All C2 traffic runs over a persistent WebSocket connection on TLS port 8443, pointed at c2.installscenter[.]com and the VPS at 38.242.246[.]176.  - The framework's get_stealth_iab_tags function profiles every compromised host across roughly 20 categories: FINANCE_ERP (SAP, TOTVS/Protheus, Warsaw, Topaz, Diebold), SCADA_INDUSTRIAL (FactoryTalk, RSLogix, WinCC), BACKUP_SERVER (veeam.exe, bengine.exe), SECURITY_EDR (csfalconservice.exe for CrowdStrike, sentinelagent.exe for SentinelOne, msmpeng.exe for Defender), LAW_ENFORCEMENT (hostname prefixes PC-, PM-, DP-, SSP-), HEALTHCARE_HIS (Tasy ERP, DICOM port 104), and DEVOPS_CLOUD (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AZURE_CONFIG_DIR, KUBECONFIG). Profiled hosts are priced and listed on Infected Marketplace at infect[.]online and infectonline[.]store with a minimum deposit of roughly USD 5.80.  - Rather than stealing credentials or cookies, BraZetsu's get_browser_intel function copies Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, and Opera SQLite History databases to %TEMP% using shutil.copyfile to bypass file locks, then runs the query SELECT url, title, visit_count FROM urls WHERE url LIKE ? against a TARGET_DOMAINS list of approximately 230 domains spanning banking, ERP, e-commerce, and government portals. The function ler_e_preparar_certificados recursively hunts the user profile and OneDrive for .pfx and .p12 digital certificates and exfiltrates them bundled in a dossier. The function obter_identidade_v8 uses regex to extract CPF and CNPJ legal identifiers. File extensions actively hunted include .cnab, .240, .400, .rem, and .ret.  - Log strings embedded in the code reference a server-side AI engine: "Coleta metadados de hardware e porte da máquina para a IA do servidor" and "Define se o arquivo é um alvo prioritário para a IA." The volume of emoji-annotated Portuguese 🇵🇹 logging ([], [], []) is consistent with LLM-assisted development. The framework tracks as AgenteV2 in prior ANY.RUN reporting, sharing loader names wifi_driver.exe and msedge04.exe, payload temp_agente.dll (equivalent to agenteV2_historico_detect.dll), identical Python 3.13 plus Nuitka build environments, and the same 38.242.246[.]176 VPS. Persistence in v1 was established via a Run key named MonitorSystem under SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run.  - Initial distribution runs through the domain caixaentradas1inboxshop[.]site using VBS droppers masquerading as a judicial notification ("processo de intimação") and file patterns msdege[0-9].exe and wifi_driver.exe. The same infrastructure distributed the Ousaban banking trojan. Buyers on Infected Marketplace can remotely execute their own payloads against purchased accesses via the _execute_worker function, creating a persistent threat-multiplication effect. Two US 🇺🇸 compromised hosts appeared for sale in April 2026, a potential indicator of geographic expansion.  Hunt priority: search endpoints running TOTVS, SAP, Senior, or Tasy for processes spawning cmd.exe (T1059.003) with WebSocket connections to external IPs on port 8443, and audit %TEMP% for copies of Chrome and Edge History SQLite databases alongside a file named debug_payload_sent.json. Flag outbound connections to Pastebin from hosts running ERP or SCADA software. Full IOC list including 16 file hashes, C2 domains, and Pastebin resolver URLs is in the Group-IB report. MITRE ATT&CK coverage spans T1012, T1083, T1217, T1113, T1027.002, and T1564.003 among others.  #DFIR_Radar

🚨 Detection Rule Friday: Suspicious Parent-Child Process Relationships  If you see winword.exe spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe, you're likely looking at a maldoc in action. If svchost.exe has any parent other than services.exe, you've got injection or masquerading.  Process lineage is one of the most reliable detection primitives we have. Attackers abuse trusted binaries (LOLBins) to blend in, but they can't hide the parent-child relationship that reveals how execution really started.  Detection Logic: Query Sysmon Event ID 1 or Security 4688 with process creation details. Filter for high-risk parent-child pairs: • Microsoft Office processes (winword.exe, excel.exe, outlook.exe) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, mshta.exe • svchost.exe with ParentImage != services.exe • explorer.exe spawning scripting engines from unusual paths • Legitimate system binaries (regsvr32.exe, rundll32.exe) launched by Office apps or browsers  Log Sources: • Sysmon Event ID 1 (Process Create) with ParentImage field • Windows Security Event 4688 with ParentProcessName (requires command-line logging enabled)  False Positives & Tuning: Legitimate macro-enabled workflows exist in some enterprises. Build a whitelist of known-good parent-child pairs specific to your environment. Document approved automation scripts. Exclude service accounts running scheduled tasks that spawn shells. Use process hashes or signing info to differentiate legitimate from suspicious instances of the same binary name.  MITRE ATT&CK: T1204.002 (User Execution: Malicious File), T1036 (Masquerading)  Start with a baseline of normal process trees in your environment, then alert on deviations. This catches everything from phishing maldocs to post-exploitation tooling.  #DetectionEngineering #DFIR

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B has been turned into a specialized local cybersecurity agent.  Meet RavenX-CyberAgent from deadbydawn101, a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-based model distilled around Opus-style reasoning and tuned specifically for penetration testing and security research.  The interesting part isn’t just the “uncensored” label.  It’s the workflow the model is designed around.  RavenX is built to work more like a security analyst than a general-purpose chatbot.  It focuses on things like:  Recon and tool-call style workflows Attack-surface analysis Structured security reporting MITRE ATT&CK mapping CWE classification CVSS scoring Pentest documentation  It also uses a RATH-style reporting structure designed to take security findings through the broader assessment process, from identifying the attack surface through analysis, impact, remediation and documentation.  That specialization matters.  A general coding model might be able to explain a vulnerability.  A cybersecurity-focused model can instead be trained to organize the surrounding workflow: what was observed, how the finding should be categorized, what technique it maps to, how severe it is and how the result should be documented.  And because RavenX is based on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, it has an interesting local footprint for a model in this class.  It’s a MoE architecture with roughly 36B total parameters but only around 3B active parameters per token.  The reported configuration supports a large context window, tool calling and GGUF deployment, making it much more practical for local security workflows than a massive dense model.  The model was reportedly trained across hundreds of thousands of security examples covering areas such as penetration testing, bug bounty reports, MITRE ATT&CK and other security-focused material.  That gives it a very different target from a normal coding assistant.  You could use a model like this as a local layer around an authorized security workflow, where it helps turn raw observations into structured findings instead of sending sensitive assessment data to an external API.  That’s probably the most interesting part of specialized local cyber models.  Privacy.  A security assessment can contain source code, internal hostnames, vulnerability details, logs, credentials accidentally exposed in output and other information you may not want leaving your environment.  Running the reasoning layer locally gives security teams another option.  Of course, “uncensored” doesn’t automatically mean “accurate.”  Cybersecurity is an area where confidently wrong output can be worse than a refusal.  So the real test for RavenX isn’t whether it answers offensive questions.  It’s whether it can reliably analyze authorized assessment data, use tools correctly, classify findings and produce reports that a human security professional can actually verify.  That’s where specialized models are getting interesting.  We’re moving from generic LLMs that happen to know cybersecurity toward models designed around complete security workflows.  Qwen3.6-35B-A3B provides the base.  The post-training provides the specialization.  Tool calling provides the agent layer.  And local deployment provides the privacy and control.  The next benchmark I want to see is straightforward:  Put RavenX through a controlled, authorized lab environment and measure how well it handles reconnaissance, evidence collection, finding classification, remediation guidance and final reporting from start to finish.  That’s a much more useful test than simply asking whether a cyber model can talk about hacking.

Towards Hierarchical Cyber Defense with Large Language Models: From Planning to Execution: An autonomous cyber defender trained with reinforcement learning (RL) is typically tied to the network on which it was trained, limiting its ability to generalize as network scale changes. Hierarchical RL reduces decision complexity by separating strategic targeting from tactical execution, but it does not eliminate this retraining dependence. We investigate whether frozen, zero-shot large language models (LLMs) can provide retraining-free control in hierarchical cyber defense and how performance changes as LLM control is extended from planning to execution. We formulate a controller-agnostic planner-executor hierarchy in which the planner selects a subnet to defend over a fixed horizon and the executor selects defensive actions within that subnet. Using the high fidelity Cyberwheel environment, with its built-in automated red team agent mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, we compare RL+RL, LLM+RL, and LLM+LLM configurations using six models ranging from 3B to 70B parameters, including two cybersecurity-specialized models, across small, medium, and large networks. Replacing only the planner with an LLM yields limited gains as network size increases. In contrast, extending LLM control to execution produces notable improvements for sufficiently capable models. For instance, a frozen general purpose 70B model holds successful lateral movement to approximately 1% of steps and attacker impact near zero across all three network scales using the same model weights, while the RL baseline is retrained for each scale. Our results show that sufficiently capable frozen LLMs can maintain strong defensive performance across the evaluated network scales without task-specific retraining, while also indicating that strong tactical execution is important to realizing the benefits of LLM-based control.ift.tt/7RLpjeq

Robinhood Chain cat-memes went vertical — VRAX +50%, Super Cat ~+750%. Ethereum scrapped its staking-burn proposal after validators chose yield over self-immolation. Porsche is winding down its Web3 initiative; 911 NFTs live on, Discord goes read-only. XRP bull-bear comment ratio dropped to 0.67, lowest since Aug. 17 — the hype is finally losing the comment war. DPRK THREAT-ACTOR PLAYBOOK  North Korea runs its cyber operations like a state budget line. Patient, persistent, and above all, financially motivated in ways that distinguish it from almost every other state actor.  The archive holds 130 documented incidents spanning September 1996 to September 2026. Thirty years of continuous operation. The program did not emerge fully formed; it grew alongside the regime's nuclear ambitions, and the two are now structurally linked. Sanctions constrain hard currency. Cyber operations generate it.  ---  METHODS AND VOLUME  Cyber Espionage: 65 incidents Advanced Persistent Threat Operations: 60 incidents Critical Infrastructure Mapping: 26 incidents Infrastructure Attacks: 24 incidents Malware Distribution: 18 incidents Ransomware Campaigns: 17 incidents Cryptocurrency Theft: 17 incidents Supply Chain Exploitation: 16 incidents  The top two categories overlap considerably by design. DPRK APT operations are the delivery mechanism; espionage is frequently the payload. What separates North Korea from most state actors is what sits below that: cryptocurrency theft and ransomware running in parallel with traditional espionage. Pyongyang does not draw a clean line between intelligence collection and revenue generation. Sometimes the same access serves both purposes.  Critical infrastructure mapping at 26 incidents deserves attention. That number does not represent 26 attacks. It represents 26 instances of documented reconnaissance. The attacks, if they come, come later.  ---  HOW THEY WORK  The operational signature is patience and cover. North Korean operators routinely maintain access inside target networks for months before doing anything visible. When they do move, it is often to exfiltrate, occasionally to steal funds, and in a smaller number of cases to stage for potential disruptive action.  The social engineering tradecraft is unusually developed. Operation Dream Job, documented as recently as August 2026, has been running in recognizable form for years. The premise is simple: contact a defense or technology sector employee, pose as a recruiter, build rapport, deliver a malicious file or link embedded in what looks like a job application process. The August 2026 iteration added CVE-2026-68820, a Windows kernel privilege escalation zero-day, to the lure chain. Same concept, meaningfully upgraded technical execution.  That combination, a well-worn social engineering framework married to fresh exploit development, is characteristic. DPRK operators are not purely tool-reusers and they are not purely capability developers. They blend.  Supply chain exploitation appears in 16 documented incidents. That number has been climbing. The logic is straightforward: compromise a vendor with broad customer access once, and the downstream reach multiplies the effort. North Korean operators have applied this across software distribution channels, managed service providers, and development toolchains.  ---  THE FINANCIAL DIMENSION  This is where North Korea differs structurally from China, Russia, or Iran.  Seventeen documented cryptocurrency theft incidents. Seventeen documented ransomware campaigns. These are not side projects. UN Panel of Experts assessments have repeatedly found that DPRK cyber operations fund prohibited weapons programs directly. The Lazarus Group and affiliated clusters have been attributed to cryptocurrency platform compromises totaling billions of dollars across multiple years. The September 2026 Security Affairs Round 597 digest captured continued activity in this space alongside document exfiltration operations, which is a good illustration of how the programs run concurrently rather than sequentially.  Ransomware as espionage cover is a documented pattern. Deploy ransomware, collect payment, but the primary objective was data access. The ransom demand provides both revenue and a convenient explanation for the intrusion that does not require the victim to acknowledge what was actually taken.  ---  INSTITUTIONAL ARCHITECTURE  North Korea's cyber operations sit under Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB), which also controls foreign intelligence and special operations. The organizational consolidation matters because it means cyber, signals, and human intelligence operations can be coordinated at the command level rather than deconflicted after the fact.  Lazarus Group is the most publicly attributed cluster, but the attribution landscape is segmented. Bluenoroff handles financial operations. Andariel has been associated with critical infrastructure targeting and ransomware. APT38 (overlapping with Bluenoroff in many frameworks) focuses on financial system intrusions. In practice the clusters share infrastructure and personnel, and the boundaries in public reporting reflect analytic conventions more than hard operational divisions.  ---  RECENT INDICATORS  The September 2026 DPRK Foreign Ministry statement is worth treating as a data point, not just diplomatic noise. Pyongyang issues sovereignty doctrine statements in coordinated patterns. They function as preemptive rhetorical cover for activities the regime knows will attract scrutiny, and they are systematically amplified through Russian and Chinese state media. The September 2026 statement coincided with documented DPRK weapons and personnel provision to Russia for Ukraine operations, an alignment that has material implications for technology transfer and operational coordination between the programs.  The Tenable-SentinelOne joint analysis from August 2026, covering 93 CVE-actor pairs, found state APTs and criminal actors converging on identical edge infrastructure vulnerabilities. North Korean operators appear in that dataset. The convergence is a deliberate feature in some cases. When your intrusion looks indistinguishable from a criminal ransomware operator's intrusion, attribution slows and the intelligence or financial objective proceeds.  The FBI's September 2026 global threat framework names North Korea alongside China, Russia, and Iran in multi-domain operations against U.S. interests. North Korea does not lead that assessment in terms of overall threat volume. China holds that position. But the FBI framework documents DPRK operations spanning espionage, economic theft, and what the framework terms transnational repression, meaning operations against North Korean diaspora communities and defectors abroad. That last category is underreported relative to its actual frequency.  ---  WHAT TO WATCH  Three things.  First, the Dream Job template keeps evolving. It has absorbed zero-days before and it will again. Any organization in defense, aerospace, technology, or cryptocurrency that is not actively training employees on this specific social engineering vector has a gap.  Second, the Russia alignment is not cosmetic. DPRK provision of artillery, missiles, and reportedly personnel to Russia creates conditions for reciprocal technology transfer. If Russian cyber tooling or infrastructure begins appearing in DPRK operations at higher frequency, that alignment has moved beyond weapons logistics.  Third, cryptocurrency infrastructure remains a primary target. North Korean operators have demonstrated the ability to compromise exchange platforms, DeFi protocols, and individual custody solutions. The sophistication of these operations has increased year over year. The seventeen incidents in the archive represent confirmed attributions. The actual number is higher.  Thirty years in, the program is larger, better resourced, and more technically capable than it was at any prior point. The financial motive is structural, not opportunistic. It does not go away when diplomatic conditions shift, because the weapons programs the revenue funds do not pause for diplomacy either.  foreigninterference.org #foreigninterference #CyberEspionage #AdvancedPersistentThreatOperations #CriticalInfrastructureMapping #InfrastructureAttacks

🚨TIMELINES, PATTERNS, THE ILLEGAL ILLICIT NETWORK & ANOTHER "UNPRECEDENTED" EVENT  👉Ninety-One Billion Dollars  On October 1, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury designated the A7 Network as a significant transnational criminal organization.  The A7 Network processed more than 2,000 transactions per day. Its total transaction volume exceeded 7.5 trillion rubles $91.5 billion. That represents approximately 13% of Russia's entire foreign trade in 2025. One network. Thirteen percent of a G20 economy's international commerce.  Treasury deployed three instruments simultaneously.  FinCEN issued a proposed rule prohibiting any transmittal of funds involving A7 Sub-Agents. That's the plumbing-level ban every bank in the world is now on notice that processing a payment through an A7 entity is a potential violation.  FinCEN issued an Alert with red flags to help financial institutions identify A7 activity. That's the map handed to the private sector the same FinCEN Exchange mechanism that briefed banks on Operation Economic Outcast two weeks ago.  OFAC designated the entire A7 Network as a transnational criminal organization. That's the nuclear option every asset, every entity, every Sub-Agent, every transaction blocked.  Three tools. One target. One press release. One morning.  Here's what the A7 Network actually is.  A constellation of purpose-built shell companies called "Sub-Agents" spread across third-country jurisdictions. Each Sub-Agent is designed to receive and send payments that make sanctioned transactions look like ordinary commerce. Falsified trade documents. Falsified import-export records. Misleading goods descriptions. The entire architecture exists to make illegal payments invisible inside the legitimate financial system.  The Sub-Agents' websites and bank accounts are controlled by A7 Network staff using custom-built VPNs that mask their true location. The companies are shells. The websites are facades. The bank accounts are funnels. The VPNs hide who's actually pressing the buttons.  This isn't a few bad actors using the financial system. This is a parallel financial system, purpose-built to evade the one that every government in the world has spent two decades making transparent.  Now read who used it.  Russia 13% of its foreign trade flowed through A7's infrastructure.  Iran  the Central Bank of Iran and the IRGC used A7 Sub-Agents to move funds through the international financial system.  Hamas  A7 facilitated transactions for Iran-backed terrorist organizations, including Hamas.  North Korea  A7 Sub-Agents facilitated transactions related to North Korean hacks of cryptocurrency exchanges.  Ransomware operators cybercriminals used A7 to move funds.  Iran's shadow fleet  one A7 Sub-Agent directly transacted with tankers, shipping companies, and front companies used to transport and sell Iranian oil in violation of sanctions. That same Sub-Agent received nearly $140 million from Iranian sanctions evaders.  Iranian weapons procurement a separate Sub-Agent transferred $1.6 million to a company linked to Iranian weapons procurement.  Every adversary this series has documented. Russia. Iran. IRGC. Hamas. North Korea. Ransomware. All of them. Through the same pipes. At the same time.  The network even built its own cryptocurrency.  The A7A5 token a ruble-backed digital token issued by Old Vector LLC, which OFAC designated in August 2025. Created specifically for A7 members to evade sanctions and transact internationally. A purpose-built sanctions evasion cryptocurrency.  Three weeks ago, this series documented a cartel mining farm in the mountains of Puebla 300 GPUs making coins from stolen electricity because the existing crypto rails were being monitored. The A7 Network did the same thing at the institutional level it built its own token because existing tokens were being screened.  When the transparent rail gets too transparent, the adversary builds a parallel rail. When the parallel rail gets designated, the adversary builds a token for the parallel rail. Each layer of evasion produces a new layer of enforcement. Each layer of enforcement produces a new layer of evasion.  $17 billion processed between January 2025 and June 2026. Eighteen months.  $91.5 billion in total transaction volume. Thirteen percent of Russia's foreign trade.  $140 million received from Iranian sanctions evaders by a single Sub-Agent.  2,000 transactions per day.  Those numbers existed inside the global financial system. They moved through banks. They cleared through payment networks. They appeared on ledgers as ordinary commercial activity. And the entire time, the money was flowing from Russia to Iran to Hamas to North Korea to ransomware operators through a network of shell companies controlled by a convicted criminal fraudster named Ilan Shor, operating from behind custom VPNs across multiple jurisdictions.  The transparent rail caught it. FinCEN mapped it. OFAC designated it. The Alert went out to every financial institution in the world. The proposed rule will prohibit any bank from processing A7 payments. The UK's National Crime Agency flagged $86 billion in A7-linked flows in August. And today Treasury tore the whole thing up by the roots.  Yesterday, the last American soldier left Iraq. Today, Treasury designated a $91.5 billion shadow banking network that served every adversary on earth.  The rifle went home. The pen went to work. And the pen found $91.5 billion moving through purpose-built shell companies, falsified trade documents, and a custom cryptocurrency serving Russia, Iran, Hamas, North Korea, and ransomware operators through the same pipes, at the same time, disguised as ordinary commerce.  Follow the pen.  The source is the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Press Release sb0644, October 1, 2026.  I am the guy on the couch, and you have been debriefed.

AI Zero Trust Revolution Artificial intelligence is transforming cybersecurity at an unprecedented pace. Attackers are using generative AI to automate phishing campaigns, create sophisticated malware, and launch increasingly intelligent cyberattacks. At the same time, defenders are leveraging AI to detect threats, automate incident response, and strengthen cyber resilience. Traditional perimeter-based security is no longer enough. AI Zero Trust Revolution explores how the Zero Trust security model—"Never Trust, Always Verify"—has become the foundation of cybersecurity in the AI era. The book explains how organizations can secure cloud environments, AI agents, digital identities, enterprise data, IoT devices, and autonomous systems through modern Zero Trust architecture.  Readers will discover how AI is reshaping cyber defense, Security Operations Centers (SOCs), identity management, threat intelligence, and the future of digital infrastructure. The book also examines emerging risks, including AI-powered cyber warfare, autonomous attacks, and the security challenges facing governments and global enterprises.  Designed for cybersecurity professionals, cloud architects, IT leaders, business executives, and anyone interested in the future of digital security, this book provides a forward-looking perspective on one of the most important technological shifts of our time.  The future belongs to organizations that can combine artificial intelligence with Zero Trust security. This book offers a practical roadmap for building resilient, intelligent, and secure digital enterprises. 做逆向时，AI 真正缺的往往不是“会不会用 IDA / jadx / Frida”。  而是：  拿到一个 APK、EXE、SO、JS 加密或 CTF 题目后，到底应该先做什么？该调用什么工具？走哪条分析路径？  最近发现一个挺有意思的开源项目：  reverse-skill  它不是单纯塞一堆 Prompt，而是给 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、OpenCode 这类 AI Agent 做了一套路由系统：  APK → jadx / apktool / Frida 二进制 → IDA / Ghidra / Binary Ninja / radare2 JS 加密 → JS Reverse 恶意软件 → Malware Analysis CTF → 专门的 CTF Skill 固件、Pwn、API Security、OLLVM 也都有对应路径。 目前仓库已经做到： • 44 条路由规则 • 175 个回归测试案例 • 45 个核心 Skill 模块 • Windows + Ubuntu CI • 不绑定某一个 AI 客户端 简单说： 以前是你告诉 AI“用 IDA 分析这个”。 现在可以变成：  你只告诉 AI“分析这个目标”，它自己判断下一步该走哪套逆向流程。  对经常用 Codex / Claude Code 做逆向、安全分析的人，这种 Skill Router 思路值得看看。 GitHub： github.com/zhaoxuya520/rever… #ReverseEngineering #AI #CyberSecurity #Codex #ClaudeCode

FortiMail's exploited flaw has no fixed build in any of four branches, and CISA's deadline is 4 October  0 of 4. That is how many FortiMail branches have an installable fixed build on Fortinet's own advisory FG-IR-26-175, read live at 11:35 BST on 3 October. Branches 8.0, 7.6 and 7.4 say "upgrade to upcoming" 8.0.2, 7.6.7 and 7.4.9. Branch 7.2 is told to move to branch 7.4, while the same table lists 7.4.0 to 7.4.8 as affected. CVSS 9.8, Known Exploited: Yes. In CISA's catalogue since 1 October, due Sunday 4 October.  🧮 Fortinet's records disagree with each other. The CVE record names 7.6.6 and 7.4.8 as versions to upgrade to; the advisory lists both as affected. The record's affected block counts 34 builds, the advisory counts 28, and they share 24. Four builds the advisory calls affected are missing from the record, so a scanner fed from it misses them.  🔍 The advisory page has changed. Internet Archive captures from 1 and 2 October show seven file indicators with MD5 and SHA-256 hashes. The live page on 3 October has none, and its timeline still says initial publication only. No revision note explains it.  ⚖️ Stated: three workarounds (switch the IBE service off, restrict webmail access, block a request pattern at a firewall) and that exploitation is known. Not stated: when it began, who is behind it, how many appliances were taken, or a release date for any fix. An archive account with a remote destination is consistent with mail leaving the appliance. That is our inference, not a finding.  🔑 If your FortiMail had been entered on Thursday, which record, held somewhere the appliance cannot reach, would show it on Monday? 🚨🤖💥🔐♾️ $ICP — AGENTIC CYBERATTACKS ARE NO LONGER A FUTURE SCENARIO.  The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure — DIVD — has itself been hacked.  And its ongoing investigation describes something cybersecurity teams need to take VERY seriously:  AN AGENTIC AI-POWERED ATTACK.  DIVD says the attackers chained TWO previously unknown vulnerabilities in Zammad.  CVE-2026-102489  CVE-2026-102490  Together, DIVD says they enabled:  🔓 Session hijacking  💻 Remote code execution  ⬆️ Privilege escalation  🚨 Zammad user → ROOT  And according to DIVD, the agentic element allowed the chain to happen in SECONDS.   But one detail is extraordinary.  DIVD found scripts containing notes where the agent appeared to JUSTIFY ITS OWN ACTIONS — including explaining why what it was doing was supposedly acceptable and “really not phishing.”  DIVD says the attack was:  “loud and very messy”  The agent was automatically deciding its next action at speed, while leaving unusually verbose explanations behind.   THIS IS THE SECURITY SHIFT.  We are moving from:  HUMAN ATTACKER → TOOL → EXPLOIT  toward:  🤖 AGENT → DISCOVER → DECIDE → EXPLOIT → ESCALATE → CONTINUE  at machine speed.  And DIVD highlighted something else extremely important.  NETWORK SEGMENTATION MATTERED.  Proper segmentation and rapid incident response helped prevent the attackers from penetrating deeper into DIVD’s systems, although DIVD confirms some data was compromised and potentially exfiltrated. The investigation remains OPEN.   This connects directly with the infrastructure conversation around $ICP.  AI agents need HARD BOUNDARIES.  Not simply:  “Please don’t do this.”  But infrastructure enforcing:  🔐 WHAT an agent can access.  🔐 WHAT identity it operates under.  🔐 WHAT operations it can execute.  🔐 WHAT requires additional authorization.  🔐 WHAT it cryptographically CANNOT do without permission.  That is why canister isolation, cryptographic identities, programmable authorization and verifiable execution are increasingly interesting as AI becomes more autonomous.  Does $ICP eliminate software vulnerabilities?  NO.  Nothing does.  But the lesson from DIVD is becoming very clear:  🤖 AI AGENTS ARE GETTING FASTER.  ⚡ ATTACK CHAINS ARE GETTING FASTER.  🔐 SECURITY ARCHITECTURE MUST GET STRONGER.  SEGMENTATION.  LEAST PRIVILEGE. sample_tweets.text: Day 62 of the restart sprint for isitdisposable.com.  Quiet Saturday, so here is a preview of the question next week's report answers, one I have never seen anyone in this industry publish an answer to: how long does a disposable email domain actually live?  Everyone treats disposable domains like a list. They are a population. Roughly 185 genuinely new ones are born every day. Some die within weeks when the provider rotates onward. Some die and come back, 1,215 resurrected in September alone. A static blocklist cannot see any of this, because a file has no concept of time.  Back in early August we started rechecking every tracked domain daily and recording each state change, knowing the data would be worthless for months, and then suddenly not. The October edition, out next week, includes the first lifespan and mortality numbers from that history. I genuinely do not know yet what the median lifespan will be, and that is the fun part. The sweep knows. We find out together.  Good data takes patience. We bought ours in August.  $0 MRR. 17 days left.  #buildinpublic

sample_tweets.text: 미국서 규제된 中 CCTV, 우리 군엔 확인된 것만 1070대  -육군 약 510대·공군 400대·해군 160대 -하이크비전·다후아 포함…군 “취약점 발견 안 돼”  최근 5년간 육군에 도입됐거나 공군·해군이 현재 운용 중인 중국산 CCTV가 약 1070대로 집계됐다. 이 가운데 하이크비전과 다후아는 미국이 국가안보 우려로 연방기관의 조달·사용을 제한한 업체다.  군은 보안점검에서 특이사항이 발견되지 않았다고 밝혔지만, 2024년에는 국산으로 알고 전방부대 등에 설치한 중국산 CCTV 1300여대에서 영상 유출 가능성이 제기돼 전량 철거한 바 있다. 군사시설 장비인 만큼 공급망 검증과 국산화가 필요하다는 지적이 나온다.  📷 한국경제·유용원 의원실 참조

군사시설에 설치된 CCTV가 단순한 감시카메라라고 생각하면 안 된다. 촬영 영상 자체가 군사정보가 될 수 있고, 네트워크에 연결된 장비라면 취약점 하나도 보안 문제로 이어질 수 있다.  그런데 우리 군에서 최근 5년간 도입됐거나 운용 중인 중국산 CCTV가 확인된 것만 약 1,070대다. 육군 약 510대, 공군·해군 약 560대 규모다. 특히 ‘하이크비전’과 ‘다후아’는 미국에서 국가안보 우려를 이유로 규제 대상에 포함된 업체다.   더 황당한 건 2024년 전방부대 등에 설치된 중국산 CCTV 약 1,300대가 합동점검에서 발견돼 전량 철거된 전례까지 있었다는 점이다. 당시 해당 장비가 중국의 특정 서버와 연결돼 영상이 외부로 유출될 가능성이 있다고 군이 판단했다.   지금 “현재까지 특이사항이 없다”는 말만 반복할 게 아니다.  군사시설에 어떤 장비가 들어와 있는지, 제조사·부품·펌웨어·서버 연결 구조까지 전수조사하고 문제가 있다면 즉시 교체해야 한다.  안보 장비는 싸다고 들여놓고 나중에 보안부터 걱정하는 방식이어서는 안 된다.  군부대 CCTV는 화질보다 보안이 먼저다. 감시해야 할 군사시설이 오히려 카메라에게 감시당하는 상황은 없어야 한다.

신한·KB·하나 등 여러 은행에서 최근 해킹 사고가 잇따라 확인됐다.  문제가 된 곳은 핵심 계좌·이체 시스템보다 대출조회, 직원용 업무지원, 영업지원 같은 외부 연결 시스템이었다.   신한은행 사고에서는 AI 기반 침투도구 사용 정황까지 나왔다.  현재까지 핵심 금융거래망 장악이나 대규모 자금 탈취는 확인되지 않았다.  이번 사건에서 봐야 할 것은 유출 인원보다 AI가 해킹의 경제성을 바꾸고 있다는 점이다.  은행에는 인터넷뱅킹과 계정계만 있는 게 아니다.  대출모집인 페이지, 직원용 모바일 시스템, 협력사 시스템, 외부 솔루션, 오래된 웹서비스, API까지 수많은 시스템이 외부와 연결돼 있다.  공격자는 가장 강한 시스템을 정면으로 뚫을 필요가 없다.  수백 개의 외부 노출 시스템을 자동으로 탐색하면서 가장 취약한 하나를 찾으면 된다.  AI는 이 과정을 빠르게 만든다.  시스템 탐색 → 취약점 후보 발견 → 공격 → 결과 분석 → 공격 방식 수정 → 재시도  사람이 하나씩 하던 작업을 AI 에이전트가 대량으로 반복할 수 있다.  여기서 보안의 구조가 바뀐다.  방어자는 모든 문을 막아야 한다. 공격자는 열린 문 하나만 찾으면 된다.  AI가 공격자의 탐색 비용을 계속 낮출수록 이 비대칭은 더 커진다.  이 문제는 은행에만 해당하지 않는다.  보험사, 통신사, 정부기관, 대기업처럼 오래된 레거시 시스템과 외부 업체 시스템이 많이 연결된 조직일수록 같은 위험을 가진다.  특히 앞으로 중요한 것은 가장 중요한 서버가 얼마나 안전한지가 아니다.  가장 관리가 덜 된 서버 하나가 전체 조직의 보안 수준을 결정할 수 있다.  이번 사건은 AI가 새로운 해킹 원리를 만들었다는 이야기가 아니다.  AI가 기존 해킹의 비용을 낮추고 속도를 높이면서, 지금까지 우선순위에서 밀려 있던 수많은 시스템이 동시에 공격 대상이 되기 시작했다는 신호다.  앞으로 확인할 것은 세 가지다.  여러 은행 공격에 같은 인프라와 AI 도구가 사용됐는지  과거 로그 조사에서 피해 기간과 유출 규모가 더 확대되는지  개인정보 탈취를 넘어 인증정보나 실제 금융거래 시스템 접근까지 시도됐는지  특히 3번이 확인되면 이번 사건의 의미는 완전히 달라진다.  AI 시대에는 가장 중요한 시스템보다 가장 약하게 관리된 시스템이 조직 전체의 보안 수준을 결정한다.

Cloudflare 要自己做 CA 了。  这件事表面上是在“给 Let's Encrypt 增加一个竞争者”。  但如果再往深处想一层，事情可能没那么简单。  现在的互联网，已经出现了一个很有意思的现象：  DNS 有 Cloudflare。  CDN 有 Cloudflare。  反向代理有 Cloudflare。  DDoS 防护有 Cloudflare。  现在，连 TLS 证书也准备自己签了。  Cloudflare 给出的理由是：  Let's Encrypt 太重要了。  每天大约签发千万级证书，服务超过 5 亿个网站。  如果这样一个免费、自动化的 CA 出现大规模故障，整个互联网可能都会受到影响。  所以需要另一个同样能够大规模自动化签发证书的 CA。  这个逻辑当然成立。  问题是：  如果解决“CA 过度集中”的办法，是再增加一个超级巨头，而这个巨头本身已经控制了 DNS、CDN、边缘网络、DDoS 防护和大量网站流量……  这到底是在分散风险？  还是把风险从一个中心转移到了另一个更大的中心？  更有意思的是，Cloudflare 这次甚至不准备从零开始建立信任。  它已经和 GlobalSign 达成协议，准备收购一个已经被大量浏览器、操作系统和设备信任的根 CA 密钥材料。  原因也很现实：  Web PKI 最麻烦的从来不是“签证书”。  而是让全世界几十亿台设备相信你签发的证书。  所以 Cloudflare 买的其实不只是一张证书。  某种意义上，它买的是一部分已经存在了十几年的互联网信任关系。  这让我觉得 Web PKI 正在进入一个非常有意思的阶段：  过去我们担心的是：  “某一家 CA 太大怎么办？”  现在可能要开始思考另一个问题：  “当 DNS、CDN、网络安全、边缘计算和 CA 开始被同一家公司的基础设施串起来之后，又该怎么办？”  当然，这并不意味着 Cloudflare 做 CA 是坏事。  恰恰相反。  多一个成熟的免费 CA，对整个 Web PKI 的冗余能力可能是好事。  真正值得讨论的是：  互联网需要的是更多 CA，还是更多彼此独立的基础设施？  这可能是两个完全不同的问题。

【サイバーセキュリティ動向分析】  2026年10月3日時点のサイバーセキュリティ動向は、AI関連コンポーネントの重大脆弱性、既知のゼロデイ悪用、パッチ適用後の運用障害、国家関連のスパイ活動、そして日本国内の制度変更が重なる局面にある。以下、直近で注目すべきトピックごとに背景・影響・対策を整理する。 GitLabの自己ホスト型AI Gatewayに、認証済み利用者による任意コマンド実行を許す重大な欠陥が確認された。識別子はCVE-2026-90970で、深刻度は9.9とされる。AI GatewayはGitLabインスタンスと外部のAIモデルをつなぐ中継サービスであり、Duo Agent Platformを利用する環境で条件が揃うと、ログイン済みの攻撃者がゲートウェイ上でコマンドを走らせられる。自己ホストでゲートウェイを運用している組織に限定されるが、ソースコードやCI/CDの機密が集まる場所だけに、侵害時の波及は開発パイプライン全体に及ぶ。GitLabは10月2日に修正版（19.2.4、19.3.2、19.4.1）を公開し、該当顧客へ即時更新を強く求めている。対策は修正版への速やかな更新、ゲートウェイへのアクセスを必要最小限のアカウントに絞ること、コマンド実行や異常なプロセス生成の監視を強化することである。クラウド版を利用している場合は影響範囲外だが、自己ホスト構成の有無を棚卸ししておく必要がある。 DellのContainer Storage Modules（CSM）では、認証を欠く重大な欠陥が複数公表された。なかでもCVE-2026-63688は深刻度10.0で、csm-authorization-storageのgRPCサーバに対し、未認証の遠隔攻撃者が登録済みストレージアレイの管理者資格情報を取得できる。Kubernetesノード上でのroot権限取得につながる経路も指摘されている。エンタープライズストレージとコンテナ基盤を結ぶコンポーネントだけに、侵害されるとデータボリュームの改ざんや横展開の足がかりになりやすい。Dellはセキュリティ更新DSA-2026-448を出し、管理者に早期適用を求めている。対策はベンダー提供の修正適用、ストレージ管理インターフェースのネットワーク分離、gRPCエンドポイントの露出確認、資格情報のローテーション、Kubernetes側の権限最小化である。 Fortinet FortiMailのゼロデイCVE-2026-104286が実環境で悪用されている。パス走査とNULLバイト処理の不備により、未認証の攻撃者が細工したHTTP/HTTPSリクエストで基盤システムへ任意ファイルを書き込める。深刻度は9.8前後とされ、米国CISAの既知悪用脆弱性カタログに追加された。メールゲートウェイは外部に晒されやすく、書き込み成功後は不正コードの配置や設定改ざんへ発展しうる。一部ブランチでは修正が未提供の時点で、FortinetはIBE機能の無効化と管理インターフェースのインターネット遮断を暫定措置として推奨し、攻撃元IPやファイルベースの痕跡も公開している。米連邦民間機関には10月4日までの対応期限が示された。対策は暫定措置の即時実施、修正公開後の適用、管理画面のアクセス制限、メールゲートウェイのログと書き込み痕跡の点検である。 ヘルプデスク製品Zammadのゼロデイ2件（CVE-2026-102489とCVE-2026-102490）が、オランダの脆弱性開示機関DIVDへの侵入で連鎖的に使われた。セッション固定によりzammadユーザーとして遠隔コード実行が可能になり、ローカル権限の不備と組み合わせてrootまで昇格できる。報告では、数秒規模で権限昇格まで進み、他サービスへの移動とデータ持ち出しが行われ、ボランティアのメールアドレスなどが影響を受けた可能性がある。攻撃はエージェント型AIを活用したものと説明されており、自動化された探索と悪用の速度が従来の人手攻撃を上回る事例として注目されている。CISAも既知悪用リストに加え、短期の修正期限を設けた。対策はベンダー修正の適用、セッション管理の強化、ヘルプデスクをインターネットから切り離すか多要素認証とIP制限を掛けること、zammadユーザーの権限監査、異常なセッション固定や権限昇格の検知である。 Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gatewayでは、未認証の遠隔コード実行を許すゼロデイ（CVE-2026-88771、CVE-2026-88772など）が実悪用された後、緊急パッチが公開された。しかしビルド14.1-73.37適用後に、特にSAML認証を使う環境でアプライアンスが繰り返し再起動する不具合が報告されている。リモートアクセスの要となる機器だけに、パッチ前は侵害リスク、パッチ後は可用性低下という二重の負担が生じている。政府・金融などへの攻撃が確認されたとの情報もある。対策はベンダーが示す安定版または回避手順の確認、SAML設定の切り分け、管理インターフェースの露出最小化、セッションと設定変更の監査、代替リモートアクセス経路の準備である。 中国関連とみられる脅威クラスタによるスパイ活動も続いている。Cisco Talosなどが追跡する活動では、Antinoと呼ばれるバックドアがOutlookやOneDriveをコマンド＆コントロールに使い、正規のMicrosoft 365通信に紛れてアジア各地の政府・政策機関を狙っている。対象には台湾、インド、フィリピン、カンボジア、パキスタン、タイ、ミャンマーなどが挙げられている。クラウドの正規サービスを隠れ蓑にするため、従来の境界型検知では見逃しやすい。影響は政策文書や連絡先の長期的な窃取、その後のなりすましである。対策はMicrosoft 365の異常なOAuth同意や外部共有の監査、条件付きアクセスの強化、エンドポイントでの不審なプロセスとクラウドAPI呼び出しの相関分析、標的型フィッシング対策の継続である。 IoT分野では、Clingと呼ばれるボットネットが確認された。コマンド＆コントロール通信をGoogleの公開STUNトラフィックに偽装し、Realtek Jungle SDK（2.0から3.4.14B）の未認証遠隔コマンド実行欠陥を悪用する。UDPパケットの先頭に特定文字列を付けてシェルコマンドを送る手法で、露出した機器を掌握する。家庭・業務用の組み込み機器が踏み台やDDoS源になるリスクがある。対策は該当SDKを使う機器のファームウェア更新、管理ポートのインターネット露出禁止、異常なSTUN様UDPの監視、不要なUPnPやリモート管理の無効化である。 Microsoftが公開した年次脅威報告（Digital Defense Report 2026）では、観測した侵入の約63％でデータ窃取が伴い、外部から到達可能なクラウド環境は平均5.3時間で攻撃を受けていたとされた。ランサムウェアの実行件数は前年比で増加し、重要製造業が標的の上位に入る。企業の多くがAIエージェントを試験導入または拡大予定であり、2028年には稼働エージェントが膨大な数に達するとの予測も示された。エージェントは新たな攻撃面になり、資格情報の悪用、過剰な権限、プロンプト経由の不正操作が懸念される。対策はエージェントの最小権限化、高影響操作の人間承認、クラウドの露出資産の継続棚卸し、アイデンティティ基盤の多要素認証と条件付きアクセス、データ窃取の出口監視である。 日本国内では、10月1日にサイバー対処能力強化法（能動的サイバー防御関連法）が施行された。15分野・約258の基幹インフラ事業者を対象に、攻撃の兆候を検知した場合の政府への報告義務が課される。警察と自衛隊は、一定の要件のもとで攻撃元サーバへの侵入による無害化措置を実施できる体制を強化する。背景には、重要インフラへの先制的・破壊的攻撃への対応力不足がある。事業者側は報告フロー、検知基準、取引先や委託先を含むサプライチェーンの情報共有を整備する必要がある。対策は対象該当性の確認、インシデント報告手順の明文化、ログ保全と政府連携窓口の整備、無害化措置が自社資産に及ぶ場合の影響評価である。 その他、cPanel/WHMでは管理者セッションの乗っ取りやrootでの任意コマンド実行を許す欠陥（CVE-2026-93698など）が修正された。全サポート版が影響し、ホスティング事業者は優先更新が必要だ。SharePointの既知脆弱性を悪用する中国系ランサムウェア集団Warlockは、水道、通信、地方行政、大学などを標的にしている。教育関連ではFrontline Educationが第三者ソフトの欠陥経由で従業員情報（社会保障番号を含む）の窃取を通知した。WordPressプラグインでも認証回避や権限昇格が複数報告されている。暗号資産取引所Bitgetでは、外部セキュリティサービスのゼロデイ経由で約3億8750万ドル規模の窃取が確認された。Microsoft公式のXアカウントが一時的に乗っ取られ、暗号トークンの宣伝に使われた事案もある。 全体として、AIコンポーネントと境界機器のゼロデイが同時に悪用され、パッチ自体が可用性を損なうケースも出ている。優先すべきは、インターネット露出の高いメール・リモートアクセス・ストレージ管理・AIゲートウェイの棚卸しと、既知悪用リストに載った欠陥の暫定措置または修正適用である。あわせて、エージェントとクラウド資格情報の権限を絞り、正規クラウドサービスを悪用する通信の異常を検知できるよう監視を広げることが、当面の実効的な防御になる。

sample_tweets.text: AI 트레이더 성장기 #013  AI 해킹이 만든 새로운 보안주 사이클?  오늘 신문에서 눈에 들어온 기사 하나.  신한은행 해킹 이후 드러난 건 의외로 핵심 뱅킹망이 아니었다. 공격 대상은 외부와 연결된 직원용 업무지원 시스템.  더 흥미로운 건 공격에 AI가 활용된 정황이 있다는 점이다.  AI를 이용하면 과거 사람이 하나씩 찾던 취약점을 훨씬 빠르게 탐색하고 반복 공격할 수 있다.  그렇다면 반대로 생각해봤다.  AI가 공격자의 생산성을 높인다면, 기업의 보안 투자도 구조적으로 늘어나는 것 아닐까?  AI와 함께 국내 보안주를 뜯어봤다.  * 지니언스 → NAC·EDR·제로트러스트 * 모니터랩 → 웹/API·클라우드 보안 * 파이오링크 → 웹방화벽·API·네트워크 보안 * 샌즈랩 → AI 기반 사이버 위협 분석 * 이글루 → AI 보안관제·자동 대응 * 라온시큐어 → 인증·접근통제  이번 사건에서 특히 눈여겨볼 키워드는 외부 노출 시스템 / 접근통제 / 인증 / AI 위협탐지.  다만 여기서 바로 매수하면 안 된다.  금융당국이 보안 강화를 주문했다고 해서 이 기업들에게 바로 신규 수주가 떨어지는 건 아니다.  그래서 이번에도 뉴스 → 관련주 매수가 아니라  뉴스 → 실제 수혜 사업 확인 → 거래대금 확인 → 차트 확인 → 주도주 선별  순서로 보려고 한다.  현재 내 관심종목은 지니언스 / 모니터랩 / 파이오링크 / 샌즈랩 / 이글루.  특히 지니언스는 올해 상반기 매출 249.2억, 영업이익 43.1억으로 전년 동기 대비 각각 +19.9%, +294.3%.  단순 테마주가 아니라 실제 실적이 따라오는지도 같이 볼 수 있는 종목이다.  AI 시대가 커질수록 AI 반도체와 데이터센터만 볼 게 아니라,  그 AI와 데이터를 지켜야 하는 보안 시장도 같이 커지는지 추적해볼 생각이다.  다음은 이 5개 종목의 차트를 비교해서 실제로 돈이 들어오기 시작한 종목이 있는지 찾아보자.  #AI트레이더 #사이버보안 #보안주 #지니언스 #샌즈랩

<사이버 안보, 사이버 방첩에 세계적 노하우를 가진 국정원이 나서 금융권 사이버해킹에 경찰, 중수청과 합동 대응해야 합니다>  통신사, 비트코인 업체, 외교부 산하기관에 이어 지금 AI에 의한 시중은행은 물론 제2금융권까지 사이버 해킹 공격 및 개인정보 유출이 동시다발적으로 발생한 것이 확인되었습니다.   경찰청 사이버테러수사대에서 내사를 시작했지만 사이버 범죄는 이제 막 출범한 중수청도 소관입니다.   국정원은 사이버 안보 및 국제 네트워크에 세계 최고의 경험, 기술, 인적 자원을 보유하고 있습니다.  국가안보를 위협하는 사이버 테러는 물론 특히 9월 29일 공포된 국정원법 개정으로 국제, 국가배후 사이버 해킹이 의심되는 경우, 국정원이 선제적으로 정보를 수집, 배포할 수 있도록 하였습니다.   현재 유출된 개인 정보는 다크웹 암시장에서 거래되어 제2, 제3의 국가적, 개인적 피해를 야기할 수도 있습니다.   개정된 국정원법 시행까지 3개월이 남았지만 작금의 사태를 테러로 규정하고 국정원을 포함한 3개 기관이 신속하게 공조, 배후를 규명해서 국민의 불안감을 해소시켜야 한다고 거듭  강력, 촉구합니다.

🚨 은행권 전방위 AI 해킹에 경찰 움직임  신한은행, KB국민은행 등 금융권에서 잇따라 보안 사고가 불거진 가운데 경찰도 관련 사건에 대한 확인에 들어갔습니다.  여기서 봐야 할 건 단순히 “몇 명의 개인정보가 유출됐냐” 가 아닙니다.  은행이라는 곳이 뚫렸다는 것 자체 심각하게 봐야합니다.  최근 기업, 통신사, 금융권까지 보안 사고가 계속해서 터지고 있습니다.  특히 AI가 발전하면서 피싱·악성코드·사회공학 공격 역시 더 빠르고 정교해질 수 있는 환경이 만들어지고 있습니다.  AI 시대에 가장 빠르게 가치가 올라가는 분야가 오히려 사이버 보안일 수도 있겠다는 생각이 듭니다.  이제는 “내 개인정보는 이미 공공재다”라는 농담이 마냥 농담처럼 들리지도 않네요.  진짜 보안에 돈 써야 할 때 입니다.  화이트해커가 필요한 시점이네요

2026년 남은 기간, 지정학에서 무엇을 봐야 할까요?  미,중 관계부터 중동, 러시아, 유럽의 대중국 정책까지 여러 갈등이 동시에 움직이고 있습니다. 다만 각국이 감당해야 하는 군사적, 경제적 비용도 커서, 쉽게 강수를 두기 어려운 상황이죠.  1. 미/중: 휴전은 이어져도 경쟁은 끝나지 않습니다  이번 트럼프, 시진핑 회담의 핵심은 기존의 불안정한 휴전을 연장하는 데 있었습니다.  단기 무역 휴전 연장, AI 사고와 위험에 관한 대화, 중국의 미국산 석탄 추가 구매, 일부 비민감 품목의 관세 인하 추진 등이 주요 내용입니다.  현재 시장은 이 휴전이 2026년 말을 넘어 2027년까지 이어질 가능성을 높게 보고 있습니다. 양국 모두 충돌을 피하면서 경제와 공급망의 취약점을 줄일 시간이 필요하기 때문이죠.  미국은 여전히 중국산 핵심광물에 의존하고 있습니다. 중국 역시 부동산 침체와 경기 부진을 안고 있어, 당장 미국과의 관계를 흔들 유인이 크지 않습니다. 다만 기술, 무역, 대만을 둘러싼 구조적 긴장은 그대로입니다.  2028년 미국 대선과 대만 선거가 가까워질수록 관계가 다시 거칠어질 수 있다는 전망입니다.  2. 이란: 미국의 선택을 제약하는 것은 탄약, 시장, 중간선거다  미국의 의사결정은 ‘3M’ 즉, • Munitions: 탄약과 요격미사일 재고 • Markets: 유가·금리·채권시장 • Midterms: 중간선거 로 볼수 있습니다.  군사작전을 지속할수록 무기 재고와 비용 부담은 커집니다. 호르무즈 해협과 홍해의 불안은 에너지 운송을 위협하고, 유가 상승은 미국 내 휘발유 가격과 정치적 부담으로 이어지죠.  중간선거가 끝나도 탄약 부족과 시장의 압박은 사라지지 않습니다. 따라서 전면전 확대보다 호르무즈 해협의 통항을 회복하는 제한적 합의를 더 가능성 높은 경로로 보여집니다.  문제는 이런 합의가 이란의 핵, 미사일 프로그램이나 역내 대리세력 문제까지 해결하지는 못한다는 점입니다. 당장의 충돌을 줄여도 재발 위험은 남아 있는 것이죠.  후티도 별도로 봐야 합니다. 이란이 영향력을 행사할 수는 있어도 완전히 통제하지는 못합니다. 미/이란 합의가 나오더라도 홍해의 불안까지 함께 끝난다고 보기는 어렵습니다.  3. 러시아/NATO: 하이브리드 공격이 확대될 가능성이 있습니다  러시아의 우선 목표는 여전히 우크라이나입니다. 동시에 유럽의 우크라이나 지원 비용을 높이고, 내부 분열을 키울 유인도 있습니다.  하지만 NATO를 직접 공격하는 것은 러시아에도 부담이 큽니다. 우크라이나 전쟁으로 전력이 소모된 상황에서 NATO의 집단방위 체계까지 시험해야 하기 때문이죠. 오히려 공격이 NATO의 결속을 강화할 수도 있습니다.  그래서 아마도 사이버 공격, 사보타주, 드론 침범, 인프라 교란, 여론 조작 같은 하이브리드 공격의 확대를 예상해 볼 수 있습니다.  이런 공격은 상대적으로 적은 자원으로 실행할 수 있습니다. 배후를 입증하거나 동맹국들이 공동 대응 수위를 정하기도 어렵죠. 다만 대규모 인명피해나 핵심 인프라 마비가 발생한다면, 더 큰 충돌로 번질 위험도 있을겁니다.  4. 미국/캐나다: 강경한 대응 속에서도 이어지는 교착상태  양국은 보복관세와 수입 제한으로 맞서고 있습니다. 다만 양측이 추가 확전의 비용을 의식하면서 교착상태에 들어갔다고 보여집니다.  에너지와 비료 원료인 칼륨 등 중요한 교역 분야가 대체로 영향을 피하고 있다는 점이 이를 보여줍니다. 이런 분야까지 충돌이 확대되면 미국도 상당한 비용을 부담해야 하죠.  미국은 멕시코와 먼저 협상을 진전시켜 캐나다를 압박하려 하고 있습니다. 캐나다는 새로운 교역, 투자 파트너를 찾으면서 미국 의존도를 낮추려 하고 있고요.  그래서 주요 정치 일정이 끝나는 11월 중, 하순에 본격적인 협상이 재개될 가능성이 있다고 생각합니다.  5. AI: 기술은 국경을 넘지만 규제는 갈라지고 있습니다  AI 역량이 빠르게 발전하면서 국제적인 안전 규칙과 개발 속도 조절에 대한 요구도 커지고 있습니다. 하지만 주요국의 접근법은 서로 다릅니다.  미국은 자율적 통제와 주별 규제가 혼재하고 있습니다. 유럽은 위험 수준에 따른 포괄적 규제를 강화하고 있죠. 중국은 AI 산업을 적극 지원하면서도 사용과 출력에 대한 정부 통제를 유지하고 있습니다.  문제는 미국과 중국 모두 상대방과의 경쟁에서 불리해질 수 있는 제약을 받아들이기 어렵다는 점입니다.  그래서 통일된 글로벌 규칙이 만들어지기보다 국가별 규제 차이가 지속되지 않을까 생각해봅니다. 기업은 시장마다 다른 요구사항을 충족해야 하므로, 규제 대응 비용과 운영의 복잡성이 커질 수 있습니다.  6. 이스라엘: 선거 이후 연정을 구성할 수 있는지가 중요합니다  이스라엘 선거의 핵심은 120석 중 과반인 61석을 확보할 연합을 만들 수 있느냐에 있습니다.  현재 반네타냐후 진영이 우세하더라도 안정적인 과반 확보는 쉽지 않을 수 있다고 시장은 평가하는거 같습니다. 아랍 정당과 협력하거나, 이들의 신임투표 기권을 통해 소수정부를 구성하는 경로가 거론되고 있죠.  다만 소수정부는 예산과 법안 처리가 어려워 오래 지속되기 힘들 수 있습니다.  정권이 바뀌더라도 팔레스타인 문제에서 급격한 정책 전환을 기대하기는 어렵다는 분석도 담겨 있습니다. 일부 정책의 변화 가능성은 있지만, 두 국가 해법을 추진할 이스라엘 내부의 정치적 여건은 여전히 제한적이라는 것이죠.  7. 그린란드: 합의 이후에도 신뢰 회복이라는 과제가 남아있다  미국, 덴마크, 그린란드 합의에 대해 보고서는 각자가 성과를 주장할 수 있는 제한적 타협이라고 평가합니다. 미국의 군사적 주둔 확대와 비NATO 국가의 군사, 광물 분야 진출 제한이 주요 내용입니다. 다만 기존 안보 체제를 근본적으로 바꿀 정도는 아니라는 해석이죠.  더 오래 남을 문제는 동맹 간 신뢰입니다. 합의문이 마련돼도 이를 해석하고 이행하는 과정에서 갈등이 다시 발생할 수 있습니다.  8. 특히 주목할 부분은 유럽의 ‘차이나 쇼크’입니다  현재 중국산 제품과의 경쟁이 자동차를 넘어 유럽 산업 전반에 압박을 주면서, 중국과의 경제 관계를 바라보는 시각이 바뀌고 있다는 의견들이 나오고 있습니다.  특히 독일 산업계에서는 중국의 보복뿐 아니라 중국 기업과의 경쟁 자체를 우려하는 목소리가 커지고 있습니다. 중국과의 관계가 자국 산업에 주는 이익과 비용을 다시 계산하기 시작한거죠.  이에 따라 EU의 대응도 확대될 수 있습니다. 개별 제품에 관세를 부과하는 데서 나아가, 특정 해외 공급자에 대한 의존도를 낮추도록 요구하는 조치가 거론되고 있습니다.  다만 유럽 역시 중국의 보복과 희토류 공급 제한을 무시할 수는 없습니다.   따라서 전면적인 무역전쟁까지 가지는 않더라도, 유럽의 대중국 정책이 더 강경해질 것으로 보여집니다.  중국 기업의 유럽 현지 생산이 타협점이 될 수는 있습니다. 하지만 유럽이 원하는 기술 이전과 현지 산업 기여 수준까지 충족할지는 별개의 문제입니다.  우리가 눈여겨볼 부분은 외교적 안정과 경제적 비용 감소가 반드시 함께 움직이지는 않는다는 점 일거 같습니다.  정상 간 휴전이 유지되도 기업은 공급망을 재편해야 합니다. 제한적 합의로 전쟁 위험이 낮아져도 에너지 운송과 인프라를 보호하는 비용은 남아 있죠. AI 협력이 논의돼도 국가별 규제 차이는 기업 부담으로 이어질 수 있습니다.  그래서 앞으로는 합의 발표 이후의 실제 변화를 확인할 필요가 있습니다.  핵심광물 수출 승인이 빨라지는지, 에너지 통항이 회복되는지, 유럽의 공급망 규칙이 얼마나 강화되는지. 그리고 이런 변화가 기업의 비용과 실적에 어떻게 반영되는지가 중요하겠습니다.

패트릭 번은 도미니언 상황이 점점 불리해지고 있다고 합니다. 에메랄드 로빈슨의 Absolute Truth에서, 폭스가 트럼프를 돕기보다 도미니언과 합의한 결정, 그리고 전날 자신이 연방 판사를 중범죄로 고발한 제출 내용을 다뤘습니다.  영상은 린델TV ‘The Absolute Truth with Emerald Robinson’ 클립이고, 제목은 “펜타곤은 선거 부정에 대해 무엇을 알고 있는가”입니다. 번과 로빈슨이 출연합니다.  화면에 2026년 9월 22일자 국방장관실 메모가 나옵니다. 수신은 사이버사령부, NSA, CIA, 국방정보국, 국가지리정보국입니다. 제목은 ‘2026 선거에 대한 외국 위협 대응’이고, 외국 세력이 선거를 조작하거나 교란하지 못하도록 국방부 정보, 사이버 역량을 우선 투입하라는 지시입니다.  번은 이 지시를 전한 뒤, 자기 소송에 대해 말했습니다. 도미니언(현 리버티보트)이 번을 명예훼손으로 고소한 사건에서, 증거개시로 나온 도미니언 내부 이메일이 보호명령으로 봉인돼 있습니다.   번은 그 이메일에 다음이 들어 있다고 적었습니다. 2020년 3월 24일, 중국 업체가 세르비아 엔지니어와 ICX 터치스크린, 402 프린터 펌웨어를 다룬 메일. 2020년 3월 30일, 스마트매틱 출신 베네수엘라 인력이 에릭 쿠머에게 선거관리서버로 가는 VPN을 열었다는 메일. 2020년 11월 3일, 쿠머가 시카고 사전투표 결과를 없어졌어야 할 WinEDS 서버에 올리고 있다는 메일. 여기에 메사카운티 도미니언 데이터 사본을 티나 피터스가 갖고 있다는 사실을 도미니언이 알았다는 자료도 포함됩니다.  번은 선거가 한 달 남았고 국방부 지시와 국토안보부 조사가 진행 중이니, 이 자료를 계속 봉인하면 사법방해와 중범죄 은닉에 해당한다고 법원에 냈습니다. 폭스 얘기는 2023년 폭스가 도미니언과 7억 8750만 달러에 합의하고 재판을 피한 일을 두고, 트럼프를 돕지 않았다는 번의 설명입니다.

(중요도 순위)  최신 사이버 보안의 관점에서 가장 근본적이고 파급력이 큰 순서대로 정리했습니다. 방어의 '기초 뼈대'부터 '행동 속도'로 이어지는 순서입니다.  1위: 제로 트러스트 (Zero Trust) 기반 망분리 역할: 기초 공사이자 최후의 보루   이유: 보안에서 가장 중요한 것은 '뚫려도 피해를 최소화하는 것'입니다. AI가 아무리 뛰어나도, EDR이 감지해도 이미 전체 망이 연결되어 있다면 늦습니다. "아무도 믿지 않고 매번 검증한다"는 시스템 구조 자체를 바꾸는 것이 0순위 과제입니다.  2위: EDR (엔드포인트 탐지 및 대응) 역할: 내부의 적을 찾는 정밀 CCTV   이유: 외부 방어선(방화벽)은 언젠가 뚫린다는 전제가 필요합니다. 해커가 내부에 들어왔을 때, 시스템 구석구석을 돌아다니는(횡적 이동) 것을 가장 먼저 발견하고 즉각 격리하는 실질적인 핵심 감시망입니다.  3위: AI vs AI (AI 위협 탐지 및 대응) 역할: 미지의 공격을 예측하는 레이더   이유: 제로 트러스트와 EDR이 잘 갖춰져 있어도, 해커가 AI를 써서 정상적인 활동처럼 위장하면 탐지하기 어렵습니다. 기존에 없던 새로운 패턴의 이상 징후를 실시간으로 잡아내려면 수비수에게도 AI 두뇌가 필수입니다.  4위: SOAR 및 24시간 자동 관제 역할: 인간의 한계를 넘는 초격차 스피드   이유: 위 1~3위의 방어 체계가 위협을 찾아내더라도, 사람이 수동으로 버튼을 눌러 대응하면 심야 시간에는 무용지물입니다. 탐지된 위협을 1초 만에 자동으로 차단하고 격리하는 '행동 대장' 역할로서 시스템의 완성도를 높입니다.  요약 1. 제로 트러스트로 절대 안 뚫리는 방 구조를 만들고  2. EDR로 방마다 CCTV를 달고 3. AI로 CCTV 영상을 정밀 분석한 뒤 4. SOAR가 침입자를 1초 만에 자동 포획하는 흐름입니다!  #보안우선순위 #제로트러스트 #사이버보안 #정보보안 #보안담당자 #IT지식 #테크트렌드

🇮🇱💙 플라이두바이(FlyDubai) 여객기 안에서 일어난 모든 일의 시작이었던, 우리의 어린 이스라엘 영웅 니나(Nina)를 소개합니다.  ​그녀는 화장실에 있었습니다.   조그만 소음이나 의심스러운 움직임에도 극도로 주의를 기울이는 여느 이스라엘 사람들처럼, 그녀는 조종실에서 들려오는 비명 소리를 들었습니다.  그녀는 재빨리 밖으로 나와 어머니에게 조종실 쪽으로 가보라고 알렸습니다.  다가간 어머니는 곧바로 "기장이 칼에 찔리고 있어요!"라고 소리치기 시작했습니다.  ​그 뒤의 이야기는 우리가 이미 다 아는 바와 같습니다...  실제로 이 모든 대처를 촉발하고 구조 과정에서 결정적인 시간을 벌어준 것은 바로 이 어린 소녀의 직관, 순발력, 그리고 용기였습니다.  ​우리의 영웅, 니나(Ha guibora shélanou, Nina)🏅 ㅡㅡㅡㅡ 인도와 이스라엘의 밀착 관계는 나렌드라 모디 총리와 베냐민 네타냐후 총리 집권 이후 전략적 동맹 수준으로 격상되었습니다.   두 국가는 지정학적 안보, 첨단 기술, 국내 정치적 이념 등 여러 영역에서 실리적 이해관계가 정확히 맞아떨어지고 있습니다.  ​1. 국방·안보 및 대테러 협력】  ​조건 없는 방산 공급: 이스라엘은 서방 국가들과 달리 인권 문제나 분쟁 지역(카슈미르 등) 사용 여부를 따지는 정치적 조건을 달지 않고 무기를 판매합니다.   인도는 이스라엘의 최대 무기 수입국 중 하나로, 레이더·드론·미사일 방어 시스템(바라크-8 등)을 대량 도입하고 있습니다.  ​공통의 안보 적대 구도: 인도는 파키스탄과 중국, 이스라엘은 하마스·헤즈볼라·이란 등과 대치하고 있습니다.   두 나라 모두 "이슬람 극단주의 및 국경 테러"를 핵심 안보 위협으로 규정하고 있어, 정보 공유와 대테러 전술 훈련에서 긴밀히 공조합니다.  ​역사적 신뢰: 1999년 인도-파키스탄 카르길 전쟁 당시, 인도가 탄약 부족에 시달릴 때 이스라엘이 레이저 유도 폭탄과 정찰 장비를 신속히 지원하면서 인도 군부 내에서 강력한 신뢰를 구축했습니다.  ​2. 기술·농업 및 수자원 관리】  ​식량·수자원 안보: 인도는 기후 변화로 인한 가뭄과 물 부족 문제를 겪고 있습니다.   이스라엘의 세계 최고 수준 해수 담수화 기술, 점적관수(Drip irrigation), 사막 농업 기술을 인도 전역의 '인도-이스라엘 농업 우수 센터(CoE)'를 통해 대거 도입하고 있습니다.  ​첨단 하이테크 협력: 이스라엘의 사이버 보안, AI, 스타트업 생태계와 인도의 거대한 IT 엔지니어 인력 및 시장이 결합하여 공동 R&D와 기술 협력을 확대하고 있습니다.  ​3. 지정학적 축과 다자 협력 (I2U2)】  ​서아시아 다자 안보망 참여: 미국, 인도, 이스라엘, UAE 4개국이 결성한 I2U2 협의체를 통해 인도는 중동 지역 내 발언권을 대폭 강화했습니다.  ​아브라함 협약의 수혜: 이스라엘과 아랍에미리트(UAE) 간의 국교 정상화 덕분에, 인도는 아랍권과 이스라엘 사이에서 눈치를 보지 않고 중동-유럽 경제 회랑(IMEC) 구상 등 대형 인프라 프로젝트를 추진할 수 있게 되었습니다.  ​4. 집권 세력의 정치·이념적 공감대】  ​힌두 민족주의(BJP)와 시오니즘(Zionism): 모디 총리의 인도인민당(BJP) 지지층은 이스라엘의 강경한 국가 안보 기조와 애국주의적 군사 작전에 강한 호감을 가지고 있습니다.  ​외교적 노선 전환: 과거 비동맹주의 시절 팔레스타인을 지지하던 인도의 전통적 외교 기조는 모디 정부 들어 철저한 실용주의와 국익 우선 노선으로 전환되었습니다.   유엔 등 국제무대에서 인도는 이스라엘 규탄 결의안에 기권하거나 유보적인 입장을 취하며 이스라엘을 실질적으로 엄호하고 있습니다.  ​인도는 첨단 무기와 기술 확보를 통해 중국·파키스탄을 견제할 군사력을 키우고, 이스라엘은 국제사회에서의 외교적 고립을 막아줄 14억 인구의 거대한 시장이자 강대국 파트너를 확보한다는 점에서 상호 보완적인 결속을 이어가고 있습니다.

📌 유출 사고 대비, 딱 하나만 한다면 이것입니다~로그 설계 기준  은행도 뚫렸는데, 사고 다음 날 우리는 무엇으로 범인을 쫓을까요?  1) 방화벽이나 보안 솔루션이 필요 없다는 얘기는 아니에요. 그런데 이번 사고에서 해커가 AI 도구인 아르텍스를 썼다는 걸 밝혀낸 건 신한은행의 로그와 공격자 IP였잖아요. 막는 장비가 아니라 남겨둔 기록이 사건을 풀었던 거죠.  2) 좋은 보안이란 절대 뚫리지 않는 것을 말하는 게 아니에요. 막는 건 언젠가 한계에 닿지만, 기록은 뚫린 뒤에도 피해 범위를 좁혀 줘요. 그래서 저는 딱 하나만 해야 한다면 로그라고 생각해요. 사고 난 날 로그가 없으면 몇 명이 털렸는지조차 말하지 못하고, 그러면 안전한 고객까지 전부 유출 대상으로 알려야 하니까요.  3) 로그만 켜 두면 충분할 것 같죠. 하지만 그렇지만은 않아요. 서비스 서버 안에 쌓아 두면 공격자가 들어와서 가장 먼저 지우는 게 그 파일이고, 지워진 로그는 있었는지조차 알 수 없어요. 그리고 로그에 주민번호나 비밀번호를 그대로 찍어 두면 로그 자체가 새로운 유출 창구가 돼요.  4) 가장 권위 있는 기준은 OWASP의 Logging Cheat Sheet예요. 저장해 두고 이 순서로 따라 하시면 돼요. 첫째, 누가 언제 어디서 어떤 고객 정보를 몇 건 봤는지 다섯 가지를 한 줄에 남기세요. 둘째, 고객 정보 값은 남기지 말고 고객 번호만 남기세요. 셋째, 로그는 서비스 서버와 다른 계정의 저장소로 실시간 전송하고 수정과 삭제를 막으세요. 넷째, 직원별 평소 하루 최대 조회 건수를 기준선으로 잡아 그걸 넘으면 알림이 가게 하세요. 보관 기간은 개인정보 안전성 확보조치 기준의 접속기록 보관 기간을 꼭 확인해 보세요.  5) 지금 우리 서비스는 어제 누가 고객 정보를 몇 건 봤는지 바로 답할 수 있나요? 그 기록을 지울 수 있는 사람은 몇 명이고, 마지막으로 그 로그를 열어본 건 언제인가요? 대답이 막히는 곳이 오늘 손볼 첫 자리고, 여러분 회사는 어디까지 되어 있는지 댓글로 나눠 주세요 ^^  로그는 평소엔 비용이지만, 사고 난 날엔 회사의 책임 범위를 정해 주는 유일한 증거입니다.  참고 링크 github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetS… #메타인지 #개인정보유출 #보안로그 #OWASP #개발자

sample_tweets.text: Argo Workflows versions 4.1.0 through 4.1.3 contain an authorization bypass vulnerability in ListArchivedWorkflows that fails to apply cluster-scoped access review when the metadata.namespace field selector uses the NotEquals operator. Attackers with namespace-scoped list permissions can use a negated namespace field selector to retrieve archived workflows from all other namespaces, exposing spec arguments, parameter values, and annotations.

Expat through 2.8.4 fails to validate low surrogates following high surrogates in UTF-16 input, allowing malformed UTF-16 sequences to be accepted. Attackers can craft UTF-16 encoded XML with lone high surrogates that consume following code units, hiding markup characters from the parser and enabling XML injection attacks.

The WP Cloud Plugins Use-your-Drive, Out-of-the-Box, Share-one-Drive, and Lets-Box plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions from 2.0 up to, and including, 3.8.3 via the download_file_to_uploads function. This is due to the import action being registered for unauthenticated users via wp_ajax_nopriv_, a missing capability check in can_import(), and the imported file's extension and contents not being validated against get_allowed_mime_types() before it is written to the uploads directory. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible.

China-linked UAT-11587 backdoors Asian government networks via Antino, a Rust-compiled implant that turns Microsoft 365 into its C2 channel, hitting at least 16 organizations across eight countries since September 2025.  Key details:  - Antino is a previously undocumented Rust backdoor supporting host recon, shell and PowerShell execution, file transfer, in-memory shellcode loading, and persistence. Its entire C2 channel runs through Microsoft Graph: it polls an attacker-controlled Outlook mailbox every 10 seconds for commands formatted as JSON in email subjects prefixed command_req_[session_id], and returns results via command_res_[session_id] response emails. Stolen files go to a OneDrive folder; attacker tools come down from a separate one. There is no traditional C2 server to block or sink.  - The delivery chain is five stages deep and leans on trusted infrastructure the entire way. Phishing emails used SPF-passing spoofed senders against targets whose impersonated domains had DMARC set to monitoring rather than rejection, so failures still reached inboxes. One lure exactly reproduced a real Taiwan 🇹🇼 Ministry of Finance ruling; another reused a real Associated Press story, with matching malware samples appearing on VirusTotal two days after the report published. The Gmail attachment preview card was recreated pixel-by-pixel in HTML to trick recipients into clicking an attacker-controlled link. From there: HTA files, Windows Script Host, a .NET deserialization gadget chain to load malicious code inside a trusted process, and final sideloading of Antino through a signed Microsoft diagnostic binary. Cloudflare Pages, R2, and Amazon CloudFront carried nearly every staging payload, keeping traffic indistinguishable from ordinary HTTPS.  - Attribution rests on accumulated technical detail rather than a single indicator. Decoy document metadata contains Simplified Chinese 🇨🇳 language tags and UTC+8 timestamps, inconsistent with Traditional Chinese-dominant Taiwan 🇹🇼 or Hong Kong. Ten separate Antino builds reference a Rust package mirror specific to mainland China 🇨🇳, a developer convenience choice, not an operational one. Talos assesses with high confidence that UAT-11587 is China-nexus.  - Scope and targeting are deliberate. Roughly 350 compromised endpoints identified across eight Asian countries, hitting defense ministries, legislatures, foreign affairs offices, border and interior security agencies, and policy think tanks. The largest single wave hit approximately 57 new endpoints in India 🇮🇳 over two days in June 2026. The victim profile maps precisely to what a national intelligence service would prioritize for collection.  Practitioner takeaway: the C2 mechanism here is the investigation's hardest problem. Antino's traffic is legitimate Microsoft 365 API calls to tenants the attacker controls, so perimeter blocks and traditional C2 detection will not catch it. Hunt for Graph API calls authenticating to external or unexpected tenant IDs, especially from processes that are not Office applications. Look for signed Microsoft diagnostic binaries spawning child processes or loading unexpected DLLs, and for mshta.exe or wscript.exe executing as part of an email-triggered chain. On the email side, audit DMARC enforcement posture across your domain portfolio: a monitoring-only policy is an open door. The Cisco Talos report contains the full IOC list and additional technical depth on the delivery chain.  #DFIR_Radar

Ransomware's first 24 hours dissected hour by hour: encryption is the final act, not the starting gun, and most first-day failures are decision failures, not technical ones.  Key findings:  - The clock started roughly two weeks ago. Mandiant's M-Trends 2026, built on over 500,000 hours of frontline investigations, puts global median dwell time at 14 days. A second finding sharpens the scope problem: the median gap between initial access and handoff to a second threat group collapsed from over 8 hours in 2022 to 22 seconds by 2025. You are often reconstructing two separate intrusion sets with different tooling and different goals, and the quiet one came first.  - Exfiltration is confirmed until you prove otherwise. CISA's November 2025 Akira advisory (co-authored with the FBI, Europol EC3, and partners in France 🇫🇷, Germany 🇩🇪, and the Netherlands 🇳🇱) records cases where Akira operators exfiltrated data within two hours of initial access, and puts claimed proceeds at roughly $244.17 million as of late September 2025. The tooling is ordinary: FileZilla and WinRAR for staging, WinSCP and RClone for transfer, Mega for cloud storage, Ngrok for tunneling. Hunt on outbound volume and destination, not malware signatures. A single host pushing tens of gigabytes to a consumer cloud endpoint over a weekend is your signal.  - Backup integrity gates everything downstream. M-Trends 2026 describes a deliberate shift toward recovery denial, with groups including those using REDBIKE and AGENDA actively targeting backup infrastructure, identity services, and virtualization management planes, including deleting backup objects from cloud storage. The Akira advisory documents the simpler version: volume shadow copies removed with a short PowerShell command. Before quoting any recovery time, restore one real file, confirm immutability or object lock is active today, and verify whether the backup server authenticates against the same domain you are about to rebuild. An untested backup is a hope, not a measurement.  - Identity is where the root cause investigation lives. The Akira advisory documents credential dumping via Mimikatz and LaZagne, LSASS memory access, and Kerberoasting against service accounts. Any of those means the credentials you are resetting were readable long before encryption started. Key questions to answer before any rebuild: which account moved first, was MFA absent or bypassed, which systems did that account touch in the 30 days prior, and do your domain controllers still hold logs covering that window. Recovery sequencing matters too: a clean domain controller in an isolated segment comes first, then data restoration into that clean environment. Restoring a compromised system in place preserves whatever persistence the access broker installed.  - Most first days fail on authority, not technique. The runbook covers isolation and forensics. It names nobody. The ransom question, the decision to take a production line offline, and the notification clock for insurers and regulators all land simultaneously on whoever happens to be in the room, and they run at different speeds on different trigger events.  Practitioner takeaway: This week, do one of three things. Restore a file from your newest backup and time it. Write three decision-makers and three deputies into your IR plan's authority section. Audit every remote access path for MFA enforcement. The Akira advisory IOC list, including the named transfer tools and VPN access vector detail, is in the report. Run your next tabletop on a Friday at 17:00 with the people who would actually take the call.  #DFIR_Radar

I'm running through a cybersecurity roles every day this month.    DFIR / Incident Responder.  This is the role that shows up after something's already gone wrong. A breach happened and your job is figuring out what, how and how bad.  You're pulling logs, checking timestamps, looking for the first point of entry and not to point fingers but to understand the full timeline; when they got in, what they touched, whether they're still in there.  Speed matters here, but so does not destroying evidence while you work. Every action you take during an investigation has to be documented, because what you find might end up in a legal or compliance process later. It's part detective work, part discipline. You don't guess, you prove.

최근 자영업자 커뮤니티를 흔들어놓은 '배달 음식 상습 협박범 자멸 사건'임.  소상공인 식당에 음식 주문을 넣고 "음식에서 바퀴벌레가 나왔다"며 사진을 보내 환불과 치료비 명목으로 매번 수십만 원을 요구하던 상습범이 있었음.  사장님이 사과하며 돈을 보내주려 하자, 이 상습범은 "인터넷에 악성 리뷰 올리고 위생과에 신고해서 영업정지 시키겠다"며 추가로 현금 200만 원을 요구하며 협박함.  근데 이 식당 사장님의 정체가 전직 IT 보안 및 디지털 포렌식 전문가였음.  사장님은 상습범이 보내온 바퀴벌레 사진의 원본 파일 메타데이터(EXIF)를 곧바로 추출해 분석함.  분석 결과, 해당 사진은 2019년 해외 블로그에서 다운로드된 이미지였고, 상습범이 조작해서 계속 재탕하고 있던 거였음.  여기서 그치지 않고 사장님은 인근 지역 자영업자 단톡방에 해당 번호와 계좌를 공유했고, 동일한 패턴으로 피해를 입은 업주 28명을 끌어모음.  28명의 피해 사례와 포렌식 증거 자료를 완벽하게 정리해서 경찰에 고소장을 접수함.  경찰 수사가 시작되자 상습범은 "그냥 말다툼이었을 뿐이다"라며 오리발을 내밀었지만, 집 압수수색에서 수십 개 업체로부터 갈취한 내역과 장부가 그대로 적발됨.  결국 상습 공갈 및 사기 혐의로 구속되어 실형을 선고받았고, 피해 사장님들의 집단 민사소송까지 이어져 통장 전액 압류당하고 파산함.  자영업자들 피눈물 흘리게 만들며 악질 협박하다가 제대로 임자 만나 인생 망한 역대급 사이다 참교육 사건임.
현재 기술 수준에서는 공격 트래픽만 보고 “이건 사람이 했다 / AI 에이전트가 했다”를 확정하는 기술은 거의 없다는... 디지털 포렌식 분야의 재미있는 연구주제가 될듯!  The agents following our injections are mostly not agents. research.opena2a.org/reports…

EVIDENCE INTELLIGENCE REALITY • HAVING THE EVIDENCE IS NOT THE SAME AS FINDING THE EVIDENCE  A significant assurance problem is becoming visible in OpenAI’s ongoing review of historical agent activity.  The challenge is no longer only:  “What did the agent do?”  It is also:  “How do you reliably find the relevant evidence afterwards?”  OpenAI has described a retrospective review process that searches large volumes of historical activity, applies automated and AI-assisted filtering, classifies potential cases, and escalates selected cases for human investigation.  That is a serious and necessary undertaking.  But it also exposes another evidence boundary:  RECORD EXISTS ≠ RECORD FOUND  RECORD FOUND ≠ RECORD RELEVANT  RECORD FLAGGED ≠ CASE CORRECTLY CLASSIFIED  AI REVIEW COMPLETED ≠ REVIEW COMPLETE  HUMAN REVIEW COMPLETED ≠ INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION  LARGE SEARCH ≠ SEARCH COMPLETENESS  This matters because evidence does not become useful simply because it exists somewhere in telemetry, logs or historical records.  In large agentic systems, evidence discovery becomes an assurance process of its own.  A stronger chain is:  REAL-WORLD ACTION → RAW RECORD → SEARCH SCOPE → DETECTION METHOD → DETECTOR / MODEL VERSION → CLASSIFICATION → HUMAN REVIEW → CORROBORATION → DETERMINATION → REVALIDATION  That means a later auditor may need to ask more than:  “What evidence supports this conclusion?”  They may also need to ask:  What data was searched? What was excluded? Which detector was used? Which model or ruleset performed the review? Which version was active? What was escalated? What may still be unknown? And who independently verified the final determination?  This creates an important distinction:  EVIDENCE PROVENANCE ≠ DISCOVERY PROVENANCE  Knowing where evidence came from is essential.  But in high-volume AI systems, organisations may also need to preserve how that evidence was discovered, filtered, classified and reviewed.  This is the layer EVELIQ Trace is exploring:  WHAT WAS SEARCHED → HOW IT WAS SEARCHED → WHAT WAS FOUND → WHAT REMAINED UNKNOWN → WHO REVIEWED IT → WHAT WAS CORROBORATED → WHAT DETERMINATION FOLLOWED  Not replacing incident response, observability or forensic systems -but helping make the evidence chain around them reconstructable.  Because in autonomous systems, having the evidence is only one part of the problem.  You also need evidence that your process for finding it was sufficient for the claim you eventually make. Apple is preparing new protections for Mac users as AI agents become more capable of accessing files, messages, browsing history, and other sensitive information stored on personal computers.  The company says it plans to tighten how apps obtain Full Disk Access on macOS, a powerful permission that can expose large amounts of private data. Under the upcoming changes, users will need to take more explicit action before an app can gain that level of access. Apple says the move is intended to address the growing security risks created by advanced AI agents that can act on a user’s behalf.  The issue has gained attention after complaints involving Meta’s Muse assistant. One report alleged that Muse accessed private messages without clear permission, though Meta strongly disputes that characterization and says the Messages integration is entirely opt-in. According to Meta, users must enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector before Muse can read message content.  The controversy highlights a broader problem facing the next generation of AI assistants. Traditional chatbots mostly respond to prompts, but newer agents are being designed to interact with files, email, calendars, browsers, and other apps. That makes them significantly more useful, but it also means a mistaken permission or poorly understood setting can expose far more personal information than before.  Another recent Muse incident raised similar concerns after a user said the assistant shared his home address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer. The user had granted Muse broad permissions, but the case showed how easily automated actions can go beyond what a person expected when an AI agent is given access to sensitive data.  Apple’s response fits with its broader privacy strategy. Apple Intelligence already emphasizes on-device processing whenever possible, while more complex requests can be handled through Private Cloud Compute. Apple says data sent through that system is not stored and is used only to process the request.  The bigger shift is that operating systems may increasingly need to treat AI agents differently from ordinary apps. Giving an application access to a folder is one thing. Giving an autonomous agent permission to search, interpret, and act on everything inside that folder creates a different level of risk.  As AI assistants become more deeply integrated into computers, permission systems, transparency, and user control are likely to become just as important as the intelligence of the models themselves.
