In the course of the attack, the suspected armed robbers killed his wife, Mrs. Wahab Rukayat, 44 years, while other occupants of the residence sustained serious injuries.  The robbers also carted away several mobile phones, wristwatches, $400 US dollars, and other valuables estimated at approximately ₦3.493 million, all at gunpoint.  Following the report and the need to unravel the circumstances surrounding the attack, the Commissioner of Police, Oyo State Command, CP Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, psc, mnips, directed that the case be transferred to the Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) of the Command for further investigation and the apprehension of those responsible.  In compliance with the directive, the VCRU commenced an intelligence-led investigation. Through sustained intelligence gathering and the strategic leverage of technology, operatives developed credible leads which culminated in a targeted operation.  Consequently, on 2 October 2026 at about 2100hrs, acting on credible intelligence generated through painstaking investigation and aided by technology, operatives were led to a suspected criminal hideout in the Sabo area of Ibadan, where three suspects were arrested.  The suspects are: 1.Akinrinola Oluwatobi, male, 28 years; 2.Okunola Mathew, male, 24 years; and 3.Ibrahim Rabiu, male, 23 years.  One iPhone 7 Plus, belonging to one of the victims of the Wofun Olodo robbery attack, was recovered from the suspects.  As part of the preliminary investigation, an identification parade was conducted, during which the surviving victims were able to identify the arrested suspects among other persons presented at the parade as members of the armed robbery gang that attacked the residence on 4 August 2026. Microsoft Threat Intelligence has identified a cluster of compromised websites leading to ClickFix attacks. Instead of downloading and executing remote payloads like the typical attack pattern, in this attack, the websites pre-fetch a script payload into the browser cache disguised as a PNG file.   When a user is later tricked into executing the malicious command, the cached website content is already on the device, loaded, and ready to be executed. This helps to hide the payload script and helps bypass the character limit of the Run dialog.  ClickFix attacks persuade users to execute attacker-supplied commands under the guise of verification or repair. In this specific campaign, a fake lure instructs users to open Windows Run, paste clipboard content and press Enter.   The injected page uses browser caching to stage the larger VBScript payload separately from the Run command. The command invokes cmd.exe to recursively enumerate files whose names start with "f_” in the browser’s profile folder such as %LOCALAPPDATA%\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles.   It compares each file’s byte length with an expected value. Rather than searching for a marker within the contents like previous attacks, it copies a size-matching cache entry to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\t.vbs, giving the cached payload a VBScript extension, then executes it with wscript.exe. Copy output and errors are suppressed. The expected size varies across variants.  The VBScript collects host information through WMI, retrieves v.ps1 from cocojambo[.]us[.]com/alfa, and launches PowerShell without a profile and with execution-policy bypass. A later PowerShell stage downloads the next-stage payload as cab.dat, then reads and executes its contents in a hidden window. The PowerShell stage triggers .NET compilation using csc.exe and cvtres.exe, then launches timeout.exe.  Subsequent payloads load .NET assemblies into memory and inject code into timeout.exe to target browser and device credentials. The injected process launches PowerShell to retrieve another in-memory stage from capsysnet[.]vg and makes outbound connections to ciliabula[.]cc.   The payload modifies the per-user PowerShell registry configuration to use the Bypass execution policy, then unpacks Python with tar.exe and creates a scheduled task that launches a Python payload through pythonw.exe for persistence.  Microsoft Defender provides layered protection across the ClickFix attack chain. Defender SmartScreen and Defender for Office 365 help block malicious sites, links, attachments, and fake CAPTCHA lures, while Defender for Endpoint detects suspicious command execution and outbound connections through alerts like “Possible ClickFix activity”. Defender Antivirus blocks malicious command execution as Trojan:Win32/ClickFix and Trojan:Win32/TermFix.   Microsoft recommends cloud-delivered, web, and network protection, application control, and PowerShell script-block logging. Hunt across browser activity, RunMRU registry key, WScript/PowerShell child processes and scheduled tasks, not download events alone. A CAPTCHA should not ask users to run code. Users shouln not paste commands from verification prompts into Run, Terminal or PowerShell and should treats such requests as potential initial access attempts.

Test anxiety is not a distinct mental condition, but the normal nervousness humans have before anything with stakes to it -- a test, a speech, a driving test, a conversation with your boss. Some students are more nervous than others, that's okay. But the push to classify this natural nervousness as a distinct condition known as "test anxiety" that requires accommodations has been widely harmful and counterproductive.  Humans manage their nervousness in all sectors of life, they must learn to manage it in school also. We should teach them how to prepare properly.  A counterargument I always see is that students have this "anxiety" because we make the stakes on these tests too high.  But to that I say: A class final exam or the SAT is not the end of the world and not "too high stakes", but by giving students superfluous accommodations on the test like 2x time, infinite extensions, or retakes, you are actually sending the message that it is more important than it is.  The message is that it's SO important for you to score well on this test we will do anything to make it easier for you to score higher, even destroy any shred of academic integrity.

Only a tiny fraction of the world’s mosquito species prey on humans. All of these are invasive across essentially their entire range, having tagged along with humans as we moved around the world. Multiple careful studies say that eliminating these species would have little or no impact on the environment. However, it would save at least a million human lives a year, and get rid of a constant source of discomfort that prevents people from safely spending as much time outside as they would prefer. Malaria is only one of dozens of diseases, many potentially fatal, spread by mosquitoes. Gene drives can safely and relatively inexpensively eliminate these parasitic insects; we can create male mosquitoes that can only have male offspring and which then crash the population. It’s well past time that we did it.

Let me tell you how I delayed WinXP SP2 for a month.  My software (BlackICE) was on the list of software that had to work. When they made major changes to the kernel network stack, my software broke.  They grabbed their reverse engineers to figure out why. What they discovered was that my software doing something evil, patching the kernel's network stack when our software was loaded. That's tricky on a multi-CPU system with warring instruction/data caches. We wrote a patent on how to do it reliably without crashing the system.  We searched through the kernel to find the location we needed to patch, looking for a certain pattern of bytes. They changed the network stack so that thing we were patching no longer existed.  So to make our software work, the inserted that pattern back into the kernel. As packets arrived, the new function would jump to that pattern, and then after, jump right back. This way, we could find the pattern and patch it -- and thereby patch the intended function.  Some Microsoft lawyers wanted to sue us for violating the software license agreement, which forbids reverse engineering, which we had to do in order to patch the kernel at runtime.  Cooler heads prevailed.  The point is our software did an ugly hack in order to work, and then Microsoft did an even crazier, uglier hack so that we'd keep working.  For years after, when meeting Microsoft engineers at conferences, they'd love to yell at me.  When Vista came along, they added signing of kernel models, putting an end to such nonsense, but also providing a real documented API we could use.

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협 환경은 AI 에이전트 및 자동화 도구를 악용한 공격이 급증하며, 특히 GitLab AI Gateway와 같은 AI 인프라의 취약점이 새로운 핵심 공격 표면으로 부상하고 있습니다([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/gitlab-patches-critical-self-hosted-ai.html)). 또한, 단순한 피싱을 넘어 공급망 공격이 다단계 C2 체인을 갖춘 정교한 형태로 진화하고 있으며, 오픈소스 패키지 저장소와 협업 도구(Slack 등)를 악용한 침투 시도가 지속되고 있습니다([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5782)). 더불어, 리눅스 커널 취약점과 같은 기반 인프라의 취약점이 실제 공격에 빈번히 활용됨에 따라, 보안 팀은 방어 실패 이후의 상황을 가정한 레드팀 훈련과 자율 대응 체계 구축의 필요성을 절감하고 있습니다([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/cybersecurity-operations/remotethreat-bets-security-teams-need-to-test-what-happens-after-defenses-fail)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **Warlock**: ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/warlock-ransomware-breach-sharepoint-in-water-telecom-operator-attacks/)) SharePoint 취약점을 악용하여 수자원 시설, 통신사, 대학 등 주요 인프라를 타겟팅하는 중국 연계 랜섬웨어 그룹.
- **China-nexus threat actor (Antino Backdoor)**: ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/antino-backdoor-uses-outlook-and.html)) Outlook과 OneDrive를 C2 채널로 활용하여 아시아 지역 정부 및 정책 기관을 대상으로 첩보 활동 수행.
- **KillSec**: ([CyberScoop](https://cyberscoop.com/killsec-ransomware-group-arrests-operation-killswitch/)) 2년 미만 기간 동안 약 500개 조직을 공격한 10대 중심의 랜섬웨어 그룹(최근 인프라 압수 및 체포 완료).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **금융권 대상 AI 자율 침투 공격**: 금융보안원은 무신사, 강남언니, 신한은행 등에서 발생한 정보 유출 사고와 관련하여, AI 자율 침투 도구를 이용한 광범위한 공격이 진행 중임을 경고하며 모니터링 강화를 권고함([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208716)).
- **통신 및 보안 게이트웨이 타겟팅**: BPFDoor, Rekoobe, AVERAT 등 리눅스 임플란트가 한국과 대만의 통신 에지 장비 및 메일 보안 게이트웨이를 공격 중([DFIR_Radar](https://twitter.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2106022326546657725)).
- **카카오톡 사칭 악성코드**: SEO Poisoning을 통해 카카오톡 설치 파일로 위장한 악성코드가 국내 유포 중([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95641/)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-90970**: GitLab AI Gateway RCE, 심각도 매우 높음(9.9), 즉시 패치 권고([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/gitlab-patches-critical-self-hosted-ai.html)).
- **CVE-2026-88771 / CVE-2026-88772**: Citrix NetScaler Zero-days, 실제 공격 악용 확인([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/)).
- **CVE-2026-87899**: cPanel 취약점, 루트 권한 획득 가능([GideonSsekidde](https://twitter.com/GideonSsekidde/status/2106340754608021761)).
- **CVE-2025-39682 / CVE-2026-53266 / CVE-2025-39964**: 리눅스 커널 취약점 3종, KEV 등재 및 실제 악용 중([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5781)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **도메인**: cyberrakshaklabs.in ([vivekkumar86538](https://twitter.com/vivekkumar86538/status/2106343212386525552))
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/)), CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2026-53266, CVE-2025-39964 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5781))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **GitLab AI Gateway 업데이트**: 자가 호스팅 중인 AI Gateway 인스턴스를 즉시 19.2.4, 19.3.2, 또는 19.4.1 버전으로 업데이트하십시오.
